§ 33.35 TOWN FEE SCHEDULE.
   The Town Fee Schedule is adopted by reference and can be found on the town’s
website.
(Res. 2024-04, passed 1-9-2024; Res. 2024-08, passed 5-9-2024)
CHAPTER 34: CODE ENFORCEMENT
Section
   
34.01   Applicability
   
34.02   Enforcement responsibilities
   
34.03   Initiating enforcement action
   
34.04   Acting on alleged violations
   
34.05   Formal proceedings
§ 34.01 APPLICABILITY.
   (A)   This chapter applies to all violations of the town code, including
ordinances, resolutions, policies and regulations adopted by the town, unless a
more specific enforcement procedure is provided elsewhere in this code. In the
event of a conflict between this chapter and a more specific enforcement
provision, the more specific provision shall govern.
   (B)   This chapter is intended to provide a uniform process for identifying,
investigating and remedying code violations and may be used in conjunction with
civil, criminal or administrative remedies as authorized by law.
(Ord. 2025-14, passed 7-16-2025)
§ 34.02 ENFORCEMENT RESPONSIBILITIES.
   (A)   Mayor. As provided by U.C.A. § 10-3b-104, the Mayor may be responsible
to enforce the laws of the town and ensure that all applicable statutes and
ordinances are faithfully observed.
   (B)   Code Enforcement Officer. The town shall designate a Code Enforcement
Officer and, under the supervision of the Mayor, shall determine when
violations exist and when enforcement action should be taken.
(Ord. 2025-14, passed 7-16-2025)
§ 34.03 INITIATING ENFORCEMENT ACTION.
   (A)   Complaints.
      (1)   Complaints alleging code violations may be made by any resident or
nonresident of the town.
      (2)   Complaints shall be made to the town offices and directed to the
Code Enforcement Officer.
      (3)   Complaints must be submitted in writing.
      (4)   The complainant shall identify himself or herself by name and
contact information.
      (5)   The identity of a complainant may be kept confidential if, in the
opinion of the Code Enforcement Officer, such confidentiality will best serve
the public interest. This section may not prohibit disclosure of the identity
of a complainant through the procedures of the State Government Records Access
and Management Act (GRAMA), being U.C.A. Title 63G, Chapter 2, Part 1, as
amended, or by court order.
   (B)   Town officials or staff. An allegation of a code violation may be made
to the Code Enforcement Officer by town officials or town employees.
   (C)   Code Enforcement Officer initiation. The Code Enforcement Officer may,
on his or her own initiative, begin enforcement proceedings if there is reason
to believe that a code violation is occurring.
(Ord. 2025-14, passed 7-16-2025)
§ 34.04 ACTING ON ALLEGED VIOLATIONS.
   (A)   Preliminary inquiry. Upon receiving information of an alleged code
violation, the Code Enforcement Officer shall first make a preliminary inquiry
to determine if there is a reasonable basis for believing that the violation
exists. The Code Enforcement Officer shall determine the most appropriate
manner for conducting the preliminary inquiry by carefully balancing the rights
of individual citizens with the public’s need for code enforcement.
   (B)   Explanation of code provisions. The Code Enforcement Officer shall
provide to the alleged violator a written copy of the statute, code, policy or
ordinance that is allegedly being violated. The Code Enforcement Officer shall
also make himself or herself available to discuss or meet with the alleged
violator to answer questions and provide information regarding the matter.
   (C)   Initial contact with alleged violator. If the Code Enforcement Officer
determines that there is a reasonable basis for believing that the alleged code
violation is occurring, he or she shall contact the alleged violator and/or the
owner of the property on which the violation is alleged to be occurring. This
initial contact may be by telephone, in writing, in person or by any other
means deemed appropriate for the circumstance by the Code Enforcement Officer.
In this contact, the Code Enforcement Officer shall make clear the nature of
the alleged code violation, attempt to ascertain from the alleged violator
whether the violation is actually occurring and request that the person remedy
or cease any violation that is actually occurring.
   (D)   Warning letter. If the violation has not been remedied or ceased after
a reasonable length of time from the Code Enforcement Officer’s initial contact
with the violator, the Code Enforcement Officer shall write a warning letter to
the violator and/or the property owner. The warning letter shall state that it
is the final warning to the violator before a formal notice of violation may be
issued.
(Ord. 2025-14, passed 7-16-2025)
§ 34.05 FORMAL PROCEEDINGS.
   (A)   Notice of violation. If the code violation is not remedied or ceased
within a reasonable length of time after the sending of the warning letter, the
town may issue to the violator a notice of violation. The notice of violation
shall be dated and shall state the name of the alleged violator, the address of
the violation, the date(s) of the violation, the town laws or ordinances
believed to have been violated, the steps the violator must take to cure the
violation, the steps the town may take to enforce the law or ordinance
allegedly violated, the penalties and fees that may be imposed if the violation
is not corrected, a date by which the violation must be corrected to avoid
imposition of penalties and enforcement action, and procedures by which the
alleged violator may request an administrative hearing as described below.
   (B)   Service of notice. The notice of violation shall be hand-delivered to
the alleged violator or posted in a conspicuous place on the affected property
or mailed by U.S. mail with delivery tracking. If these methods are
unsuccessful in reaching the person, notice may be published in a newspaper of
general circulation in the town.
   (C)   Response to notice of violation and request for hearing. A person who
receives a notice of violation has a right to an administrative hearing. To
receive a hearing, the alleged violator must request a hearing in writing to
the Town Recorder/Clerk. The request for hearing must be received by the town
before the end of the tenth business day after the person’s receipt of, or
posting or publication of, the notice of violation. If no written request for
hearing is received by the town within this time, the allegation in the notice
of violation will be deemed by the town to be true and to be the final
administrative order of the town on the matter, the right to administrative
appeal will be waived and penalties and enforcement measures will be imposed.
   (D)   Administrative hearing. Within 45 days of receiving a written request
for hearing, the town shall hold an administrative hearing. The hearing shall
be conducted by an Administrative Law Judge appointed by the Mayor with the
advice and consent of the Town Council. The Administrative Law Judge may not be
an employee of the town.
      (1)   Notice of the hearing shall be given at least 14 days prior to the
hearing. An alleged violator who fails to appear at an administrative hearing
after proper notice shall waive the right to an administrative hearing as if no
hearing had been requested.
      (2)   The hearing shall be a public meeting. The hearing shall be
recorded or otherwise documented so that a true and correct transcript may be
made of its proceedings.
      (3)   Both the town and the alleged violator shall have the opportunity
to speak and to call witnesses at the hearing. The Administrative Law Judge may
allow competent evidence and documents to be introduced at the hearing without
observance of formal rules of evidence or procedure. Each side shall be allowed
to question and cross-examine witnesses. Each side may be represented by an
attorney, but if the alleged violator is to be represented by an attorney, that
attorney shall contact the Town Attorney at least two business days prior to
the hearing.
      (4)   The town shall bear the burden of proof to establish the existence
of a violation. Such proof shall be established by a preponderance of the
evidence.
      (5)   At the conclusion of the hearing, or within five business days
thereafter, the Administrative Law Judge shall issue a written order. The order
shall find that the violation has or has not occurred. If the order finds that
the violation has not occurred, the proceeding shall be dismissed. If the order
finds that the violation has occurred, the order may impose penalties as
provided in this or other town ordinances. The order may also direct the
violator to cease and desist from the violation, and may direct the town to
abate the violation on its own as necessary. The order may give interim or
temporary directives as necessary, and may also embody agreements the two sides
may make before, during or after the hearing.
   (E)   Abatement. If the order issued after the administrative hearing finds
that a violation has occurred, or if no hearing was requested, the town shall
have authority to take reasonable measures to abate the violation as specified
in the order or notice of violation, including entering onto the property at
the site of the violation and physically abating the violation.
   (F)   Emergency abatement. Nothing in this chapter shall be construed to
prohibit the town from taking emergency measures to immediately abate a
violation when preservation of the life, safety or health of the public
requires immediate action.
   (G)   Recordation. The town may record the order issued by the
Administrative Law Judge, or, if no hearing was requested, the notice of
violation, with the County Recorder, indexed to the property (if any) at which
the violation occurred. If an order or notice is so recorded, and the violation
is thereafter abated and the property comes into compliance, the town shall
file with the County Recorder a notice of compliance retracting the stated
violation within 30 days of the violation coming into compliance.
   (H)   Appeals. Any person adversely affected by an administrative order
issued following an administrative hearing under this chapter may petition a
State District Court for review of the order pursuant to U.C.A. § 10-3-703.7,
within 30 days of the issuance of the order.
   (I)   Remedies not exclusive. The existence or use of the procedures
described in this section shall not preclude the use by the town of other
enforcement mechanisms unless prohibited by law.
(Ord. 2025-14, passed 7-16-2025)
§ 34.99 PENALTY.
   If the order issued after the administrative hearing finds that a violation
has occurred, or if no hearing was requested, the town may impose penalties as
specified in the law or ordinance found violated. In the absence of another
applicable penalty provision, the town may impose a penalty not to exceed the
maximum fine for a Class B misdemeanor under state law per day of violation. In
addition, the violator shall be assessed and required to pay all costs actually
incurred by the town in abating and enforcing the law or ordinance in the case,
and in holding the administrative hearing, if one was held, including, but not
limited to, inspection costs, filing fees, title searches, equipment costs,
attorneys’ fees and Administrative Law Judge fees.
(Ord. 2025-14, passed 7-16-2025)

**** CULINARY WATER DISTRIBUTION SYSTEM ****
§ 50.30 OWNERSHIP AND PURPOSE.
   The town owns and operates a culinary water distribution system (“system”)
for the purpose of furnishing culinary water to residents and businesses within
the town. This subchapter governs the operation, connection, expansion and
protection of the system, superseding any conflicting provisions in prior
ordinances. This subchapter is adopted pursuant to U.C.A. Title 10, Chapter 8
(Municipal Utilities), U.C.A. Title 73 (Water and Irrigation).
(Ord. 2025-15, passed 9-17-2025)
§ 50.31 IRRIGATION COMPANY.
   (A)   A separate legal entity that operates independently from the town. The
company retains fiduciary responsibility for 40 grandfathered shares existing
at the time of the town’s purchase of the culinary water system, which remain
subject to their original agreements. The company maintains its own water
rights, irrigation shares and rules of operation. The town does not regulate,
control or guarantee water service provided by the company, and all questions,
disputes or service issues related to the irrigation system shall be addressed
directly with the company.
   (B)   All company culinary water shares that have been transferred to the
town shall be administered in accordance with the court decree of 1965. Owners
of such shares acknowledge that water use, allocation and priority are governed
by the terms of said decree, and that the town shall manage these shares
subject to its provisions.
(Ord. 2025-15, passed 9-17-2025)
§ 50.32 SYSTEM GOALS.
   The culinary water system shall be managed to:
   (A)   Protect public health, safety and welfare;
   (B)   Provide adequate water for existing and future needs consistent with
the general plan;
   (C)   Ensure capacity for fire suppression in accordance with the State Fire
Marshal’s standards and NFPA 24/1142, as amended;
   (D)   Maintain orderly and efficient system design;
   (E)   Preserve water quality and prevent contamination; and
   (F)   Protect the rural character, resources and value of the town.
(Ord. 2025-15, passed 9-17-2025)
§ 50.33 DIRECTOR OF WATER DEPARTMENT.
   A Director of Water Department is appointed to oversee the system, enforce
this subchapter and administer the cross-connection control program. The
Director shall coordinate with the Town Engineer and Town Council on all
capacity determinations, fire flow requirements and water rights transfers.
(Ord. 2025-15, passed 9-17-2025)
§ 50.34 DEFINITIONS.
   For the purpose of this subchapter, the following definitions shall apply
unless the context clearly indicates or requires a different meaning. Where
definitions differ from or are not provided in this section, the definitions
contained in U.C.A. Title 73 (Water and Irrigation), State Administrative Code
R309 (Drinking Water) or applicable federal standards shall apply.
   ACRE-FOOT (AF). The volume of water required to cover one acre of land to a
depth of one foot, equal to 325,851 gallons.
   APPLICANT. Any individual, developer, corporation or entity applying for
connection, subdivision approval or any service under this subchapter.
   BACKFLOW PREVENTION ASSEMBLY. A device installed to prevent contamination of
the town’s water system.
   BUILDING OFFICIAL. The official responsible for ensuring compliance with
construction and utility regulations.
   CAPACITY REVIEW. The evaluation performed by the Town Engineer to determine
whether the culinary water system has sufficient source capacity, storage
capacity and distribution capacity to serve a proposed development, including
fire flow requirements.
   CEDAR VALLEY AQUIFER. The designated groundwater basin from which the town’s
municipal and culinary water rights are sourced, located in State Water Rights
Area 54.
   CHANGE APPLICATION. An application filed with the State Engineer to change
the point of diversion, place of use or nature of use of a water right.
   CONNECTION (OR SERVICE CONNECTION). The physical tie-in of a property or
structure to the town’s culinary water system, including the service line,
meter and appurtenances.
   CROSS-CONNECTION. Any physical connection or arrangement between the town’s
culinary water system and another water source, including a private well,
irrigation system or secondary water system, through which backflow could occur
into the town system.
   CULINARY WATER. Potable water that meets all applicable State Department of
Environmental Quality (DEQ) and State Division of Drinking Water (DOW)
standards for human consumption, domestic use and food preparation.
   CUSTOMER. Any person, business or entity receiving water service from the
town.
   DELINQUENT ACCOUNT. An account with an outstanding balance beyond the due
date as defined in §
50.38(A).
   DEVELOPER. Any person, partnership, corporation or entity proposing to
subdivide land, construct improvements or connect to the town’
   DIRECTOR OF WATER DEPARTMENT. The individual appointed by the Town Council
to oversee the town’s culinary water system, enforce this subchapter and
coordinate with the Town Engineer.
   FAIRFIELD IRRIGATION COMPANY or COMPANY.
      (1)   A separate legal entity that operates independently from the town.
      (2)   FAIRFIELD IRRIGATION COMPANY is a nonprofit company established for
the equitable distribution of water issuing forth from a natural flowing spring
thus providing irrigation, stock watering and culinary for shareholders within
said company
   FAIRFIELD IRRIGATION CULINARY SHARE. An irrigation culinary water share that
is governed by the Fairfield Irrigation Company. These SHARES are not available
to purchase.
   FINAL PLAT. A subdivision map approved by the Town Council and recorded with
the county, which identifies all lots, dedications, easements and water rights
conveyed.
   IMPACT FEES. Charges assessed in accordance with the town’s impact fee
facilities plan and impact fee analysis to ensure new development pays its
proportionate share of system-level improvements.
   LIVESTOCK WATERING PERMIT. A temporary water permit issued by the town for
the limited purpose of watering livestock, subject to metering, duration limits
and prohibitions on irrigation of fields or land.
   MAIN LINE (WATER MAIN). A water distribution pipeline owned and maintained
by the town, generally located within a public right-of-way or utility
easement, from which service connections are made.
   MASTER DEVELOPMENT AGREEMENT (MDA). A written agreement between a developer
and the town that governs water service obligations, infrastructure
installation, water right conveyances, reimbursement terms and other conditions
of development approval.
   METER. A device owned and maintained by the town to measure culinary water
delivered to a service connection.
   METER TAMPERING. Any unauthorized interference, bypass, removal or
modification of a town-owned meter, meter box or appurtenance.
   MUNICIPAL OR CULINARY WATER RIGHT. A groundwater right authorized by the
State Engineer for municipal or culinary use and approved for diversion at the
town’s designated points of diversion.
   PERFORMANCE GUARANTEE. A bond, escrow, letter of credit or other acceptable
security required by the town to ensure completion of improvements or transfer
of water rights.
   PLATTED LOT. A parcel of land that has received final subdivision approval
and has been recorded with the county.
   POINT OF DIVERSION. The legally authorized location where water under a
valid right may be diverted from its natural source.
   PRIVATE WELL. A groundwater well owned and operated by a private individual
or entity, not incorporated into the town’s culinary water system.
   SECONDARY USE. The use of water from a private well or non-culinary source
for purposes other than indoor household culinary use, such as outdoor
irrigation, livestock watering or agricultural purposes, provided such use
complies with all applicable state water right and cross-connection
regulations.
   SERVICE LINE. The pipe and related infrastructure running from the town’s
main to the customer’s meter and from the meter to the building served.
   SHORT-TERM WATER PERMIT. A permit issued by the town for temporary water use
such as construction, dust control or livestock watering. Such permits shall
not exceed 90 days, must be metered and do not establish permanent service
rights.
   SUBDIVISION. Any division of land requiring town approval under the town’s
subdivision ordinance.
   SYSTEM (CULINARY WATER SYSTEM). The complete culinary water distribution
system owned and operated by the town, including sources, wells, pumps, storage
tanks, mains, service connections and meters.
   TOWN ENGINEER. The professional engineer designated by the town to review,
approve and inspect all water-related plans, improvements and water right
transfers.
   UNAUTHORIZED USE. Any use of the town water system without proper
authorization, including unmetered consumption or bypassing a meter.
   UNAUTHORIZED USER. Any person who obtains water service from the town system
without proper authorization, permit or connection approval.
   USER. Any individual, household or business that consumes or receives water
service.
   WASTEFUL USE. Excessive or negligent water usage that leads to avoidable
waste, as outlined in §
50.42.
   WATER BANKING. The conveyance of water rights to the town for retention and
future use on a specific parcel or project, subject to a Town Council-approved
development agreement.
   WATER DIRECTOR. The town official responsible for overseeing the
administration and operation of the municipal water system.
   WATER MAIN. A principal pipeline owned and maintained by the town that
distributes water to customers.
   WATER MAIN EXTENSION. A newly constructed segment of water main designed to
connect a development to the existing town system, required to meet town
standards.
   WATER METER. A device used to measure the quantity of water used by a
customer.
   WATER RIGHT. A right to divert and beneficially use water under state law,
recognized by the State Engineer.
   WATER SERVICE CONNECTION. The physical connection between a user’s plumbing
system and the town’s water system.
   WELL CAPPING. The permanent sealing of a groundwater well in compliance with
State Administrative Code R655-9 (Water Well Drilling) when required by this
subchapter or as a condition of connection to the town system.
(Ord. 2025-15, passed 9-17-2025)
§ 50.35 FUNDAMENTAL POLICIES.
   (A)   No irrigation shares in the culinary system. Irrigation water shares,
secondary water shares or any other non-culinary water rights shall not be
accepted into the town’s culinary system. Surface water or agricultural shares
shall not be accepted unless certified as municipal/culinary by the State
Engineer and approved by the town’s designated water engineer.
   (B)   Water rights source and location. All water rights must be transferred
to the town’s approved point of diversion from the Cedar Valley aquifer and
determined to be culinary water before being moved.
   (C)   Water rights review. All water rights offered to the town must be
reviewed by the town’s designated water engineer for suitability, quantity and
transferability before acceptance.
   (D)   Developer cost responsibility. Developers shall connect and bear 100%
of the cost of extending and connecting water lines, tanks, pump stations and
related equipment necessary to serve their development from the nearest
approved connection point. Impact fees are in addition to, not in lieu of,
these direct costs.
   (E)   Impact fees.
      (1)   All developments shall pay the applicable impact fees listed in the
Town Fee Schedule for each culinary water connection.
      (2)   Each lot shall require a separate connection and corresponding
impact fee.
      (3)   Impact fees have been established pursuant to an impact fee study
and shall remain in effect unless amended by the town in accordance with state
law.
   (F)   Cross-connection prohibition. Under no circumstances shall a private
well or any other secondary water source be cross-connected with the town’s
culinary water system, including any connection to a residence, accessory
dwelling unit (ADU) or accessory structure.
(Ord. 2025-15, passed 9-17-2025) Penalty, see §
50.99
§ 50.36 WELL CAPPING AND CROSS-CONNECTION REQUIREMENTS.
   (A)   Voluntary connection. When a property owner voluntarily connects to
the town’s culinary water system and transfers the water right associated with
an existing well to the town, the well shall be permanently capped and
abandoned in compliance with state standards.
   (B)   Subdivision or annexation. In the case of new subdivisions,
annexations or system expansions where properties are required to connect to
the town’s culinary water system as a condition of approval, existing wells on
those properties shall be required to be capped in accordance with state
standards.
   (C)   Existing independent wells. Nothing in this section shall be construed
to require existing property owners who remain independent of the town’s
culinary water system to cap or abandon their lawful private wells.
   (D)   Cross-connection prohibition. 
      (1)   Where a property is served by the town’s culinary water system, no
private well shall be physically connected to the household plumbing or to any
portion of the town’s culinary water system.
      (2)   Any retained wells may only be used for approved secondary purposes
(such as outdoor irrigation or livestock watering), and such uses must comply
with all applicable state cross-connection and backflow prevention regulations.
(Ord. 2025-15, passed 9-17-2025) Penalty, see §
50.99
§ 50.37 WATER SHARE REQUIREMENTS.
   (A)   Required volumes by land use.
      (1)   All applicants must convey adequate water rights to the town prior
to final plat approval (for subdivisions) or prior to issuance of a building
permit (for single-lot development), except as allowed under §
50.39.

   (B)   Platted water disclosure. All final plats shall note the volume of

   (C)   Right to require more water. If anticipated demand exceeds volumes

   (D)   Low water or non-water use businesses. In cases where a business or

communications facilities or similar operations), the Town Council may, at its

and/or impact fee requirements. Such determinations shall be made on a case-by-
case basis, proportionate to the actual anticipated water demand and documented
in the development approval.
   (E)   Reduction of water right requirement. The Town Council may, at its
sole discretion, reduce the amount of required water rights if the applicant
provides adequate proof, supported by engineering or professional analysis,
that the full requirement is not necessary to serve the intended use. Any such
reduction shall be documented in the approval of the development or connection.
   (F)   Nothing in this subchapter obligates the town to approve a connection
if system capacity is insufficient.
(Ord. 2025-15, passed 9-17-2025) Penalty, see §
50.99
§ 50.38 OUTDOOR IRRIGATION AND ANIMAL UNIT REGULATIONS.
   (A)   Outdoor irrigation.
      (1)   Culinary water connections may be used for outdoor landscaping
irrigation on an area not to exceed one-tenth acre per acre foot of water
right.
      (2)   Irrigation of agricultural fields, pastureland or similar large-
scale areas is prohibited on the town’s culinary water system.
   (B)   Animal units by lot size.
      (1)   Lots one acre or less: up to three animal units may be maintained.
      (2)   Lots two to five acres: up to six animal units may be maintained,
provided that each lot has a minimum of one and one-tenth acre-feet of water
rights dedicated for such use (in accordance with § 
50.37).
      (3)   Lots greater than five acres: animal allowances shall be governed
by the provisions of the Agricultural Zone regulations.
   (C)   Animal unit equivalents. For purposes of this section, the following
equivalencies shall apply:
      (1)   One cow or horse equals one animal unit;
      (2)   Five sheep or goats equals one animal unit;
      (3)   Twenty-five chickens, ducks or similar fowl equals one animal unit;
and
      (4)   Other species shall be evaluated by the town on a case-by-case
basis, based on equivalent water consumption and space requirements.
(Ord. 2025-15, passed 9-17-2025) Penalty, see §
50.99
§ 50.39 TIMING OF WATER RIGHT TRANSFER.
   (A)   Single lot residential requirements.
      (1)   Initiation and review. The applicant shall initiate the transfer of
required water rights; and submit water rights for review by the town’s
designated water engineer, who shall verify their suitability for use in the
town’s culinary water system.
      (2)   Building permit condition. No building permit shall be issued until
the Town Engineer has approved the proposed transfer of water rights.
      (3)   Deeding and state approval. Following Town Engineer approval, the
applicant shall deed the approved water rights to the town and obtain approval
from the State Engineer to change the point of diversion to the town’s
designated point of diversion.
      (4)   Single-family dwelling requirement. For the construction of a
single-family dwelling, the approved water right must be fully transferred into
the town’s culinary water system or into an approved town-owned well, before a
certificate of occupancy will be issued.
      (5)   Source limitation exception.
         (a)   Water rights transferred to the town shall be municipal or
culinary well rights from State Water Rights Area 54 (Cedar Valley).
         (b)   In rare cases, the town may accept water rights from another
water rights area if the State Engineer determines, in writing, that the rights
are suitable for transfer to the town’s culinary water system and the town’s
designated water engineer approves their use.
   (B)   Subdivision/multi-lot residential water right transfer requirements.
      (1)   All residential subdivisions shall transfer to the town, prior to
final plat approval, a minimum of one acre-foot of approved municipal or
culinary water rights from State Water Rights Area 54 for each one acre lot, or
the amount otherwise required for the lot size under §
50.37.
      (2)   Water rights may be transferred in phases corresponding to the
recorded plat phases; however, no subdivision phase shall receive final plat
approval until all required water rights for that phase have been transferred
to the town.
   (C)   Performance guarantee requirement. For phased subdivisions, the Town
Council may require a bond, escrow or other financial guarantee to ensure
delivery of all required water rights for subsequent phases.
      (1)   Initiation and review. For each subdivision or phase of
subdivision, the developer shall initiate the transfer of the required water
rights for all lots in that phase and submit them to the town’s designated
water engineer for review. The Town Engineer shall verify that the water rights
are suitable for use in the town’s culinary water system.
      (2)   State approval and deeding.
         (a)   After Town Engineer approval, developer shall obtain approval
from the State Engineer to change the point of diversion to the town’s
designated point of diversion.
         (b)   The developer shall deed the approved water rights to the town.
      (3)   Final plat condition. No final plat approval for any phase or for
an entire subdivision shall be recorded until all required water rights for
that phase or development have been approved by the state engineer and the
change of diversion into the town has been completed.
      (4)   Source limitation exception. Water rights transferred to the town
shall be municipal or culinary water rights from State Water Rights Area 54
(Cedar Valley). In rare cases, the town may accept water rights from another
water rights area if the State Engineer determines, in writing, that the rights
have been approved for transfer to the town’s culinary water system and the
town’s designated water engineer approves their use.
   (D)   Commercial and industrial water rights requirements.
      (1)   Initial proof at site plan approval. At the time of site plan
approval, the developer shall provide proof of ownership of municipal or
culinary well rights from State Water Rights Area 54 (Cedar Valley) in no less
than the minimum amount required for the proposed zoning:
         (a)   Commercial/retail: one and eight-tenths acre-feet per lot of
developed land;
         (b)   Light industrial: nine-tenths acre-feet per lot of developed
land; and
         (c)   Non-standard uses: determined by the town’s designated water
engineer’s based anticipated demand.
      (2)   Final determination at time of building permit or business license
application.
         (a)   Prior to issuance of a building permit (or a business license if
no building permit is required), the applicant shall submit final water use
estimates to the town’s designated water engineer.
         (b)   If the final requirement exceeds the minimum provided at site
plan approval, the applicant shall transfer the additional water rights to the
town before the permit or license is issued.
      (3)   Building permit issuance. All required water rights must be fully
transferred to the town and approved by the State Engineer, with the point of
diversion changed to the town’s designated point of diversion, before a
building permit can be issued.
      (4)   Water banking option. If a developer wishes to bank water rights
for future use on the same parcel, the terms and conditions for banking shall
be set forth in a written development agreement approved by the Town Council.
Banked rights must be held by the town not by the developer, privately, to
ensure the town retains control.
      (5)   No reliance on town owned water rights. The town does not maintain
excess water rights for allocation to new commercial or industrial
developments. Developers are solely responsible for acquiring and transferring
adequate rights for their projects.
   (E)   Single commercial or light industrial user requirements.
      (1)   Initiation and review. The applicant shall initiate the transfer of
required water rights and submit them for review by the town’s designated water
engineer, who shall verify their suitability for use in the town’s culinary
water system.
      (2)   Building permit condition. No building permit shall be issued until
the Town Engineer has approved the proposed transfer of water rights.
      (3)   Deeding and state approval. The state will approve the point of
diversion before the water can be moved or deeded to the town. The water point
of diversion shall be changed to the town’s point of diversion.
      (4)   Approved water right. The approved water right must be fully
transferred into the town’s culinary water system, or into an approved town
owned well, before a certificate of occupancy will be issued.
(Ord. 2025-15, passed 9-17-2025)
§ 50.40 WATER MAIN LINE EXTENSIONS.
   (A)   Connection point and alignment. All water main line extensions shall
originate from the nearest adequate, existing main line and extend across the
full frontage of the development along all public street frontages, in
accordance with the town’s master water plan.
   (B)   Plans and approvals. No person shall construct a water main line
extension without first submitting detailed plans to the Town Engineer for
review and receiving written approval. The applicant shall be bound by all
applicable town ordinances, resolutions, regulations and construction
specifications. All installations shall comply with current American Water
Works Association (AWWA) standards.
   (C)   Construction standards. All work shall be performed by a licensed,
bonded and insured contractor, inspected in accordance with town standards.
   (D)   Boring requirements. Boring of pipelines under paved roadways is
required unless the Town Council determines otherwise due to extenuating
circumstances. The cost of boring shall be the developer’s responsibility.
   (E)   Developer costs. The developer shall bear all costs associated with
the extension, including but not limited to: installation of the new water
main, road restoration, utility relocation, easements, replacement of any
infrastructure, landscaping or other improvements damaged or removed during
construction.
   (F)   Voluntary extensions and system level improvements. A developer may
voluntarily extend a water main line beyond the distance required for their
project.
      (1)   If the extension is identified as a system-level improvement in the
town’s master water plan, the town shall provide an impact fee credit equal to
the cost of that improvement.
      (2)   If the cost exceeds the developer’s impact fee liability, the town
and developer may negotiate a reimbursement agreement for the excess cost,
subject to Town Council approval.
   (G)   Fire protection and water right requirement. All structures requiring
fire protection or culinary service shall be supported by adequate municipal or
culinary water rights. Where extension of a waterline is necessary to provide
fire hydrants or service to such structures, the developer or property owner
shall transfer to the town an adequate water right from State Water Rights Area
54. The quantity of water right transferred shall be sufficient to meet both
the fire flow and domestic water capacity needs of the development, as
determined by the Town Engineer in consultation with the Fire Authority.
   (H)   Transfer of water rights. No building permit, subdivision approval,
occupancy or system connection shall be granted until the necessary water
rights have been transferred and all required waterline extensions have been
completed in compliance with town standards.
(Ord. 2025-15, passed 9-17-2025) Penalty, see §
50.99
§ 50.41 MASTER DEVELOPMENT AGREEMENTS.
   (A)   An MDA is required for any development requiring a water system
extension.
   (B)   The MDA must:
      (1)   Define project scope, capacity and infrastructure specifications;
      (2)   Establish reimbursement terms (if any) approved in writing before
construction;
      (3)   Limit reimbursement eligibility to town-approved system-level
improvements; and
      (4)   Set duration of reimbursement period (maximum ten years).
(Ord. 2025-15, passed 9-17-2025)
§ 50.42 PRIVATE SYSTEMS AND WELLS.
   (A)   Private wells for culinary use. Private wells are prohibited for
culinary use unless:
      (1)   The lot is more than 300 feet from the existing municipal water
system;
      (2)   The Town Council determines that the private well aligns with the
town’s land use goals and that connection to the municipal system is cost-
prohibitive; and
      (3)   The well meets all state standards and remains on the same parcel
as the served building.
   (B)   Connections. Connection to the municipal system may be required by the
Town Council if system expansion renders service to new construction reasonably
available.
   (C)   Town option to extend service. In cases where a lot is more than 300
feet from the existing system, the town may, at its sole discretion, choose to
cover the additional cost of extending the municipal waterline and require the
property owner to connect to the system instead of drilling a private well.
   (D)   Agricultural wells. Agricultural wells are permitted if:
      (1)   The lot is ten acres or larger;
      (2)   The water rights are agricultural in nature; and
      (3)   All required state and county approvals are obtained.
(Ord. 2025-15, passed 9-17-2025) Penalty, see §
50.99
§ 50.43 WATER AND WATER LINE REGULATIONS AND RESTRICTIONS.
   (A)   Water use restrictions. The Mayor, with Town Council approval, may
issue a proclamation restricting the use of water during times of emergency.
Such proclamation shall be signed by the Mayor and remain in effect until
rescinded.
   (B)   Water source protection plan.
      (1)   The town’s culinary water source protection zones are subject to
change based on updated studies and regulatory requirements. Residents and
property owners located within these areas shall refer to the most current
Source Protection Zone plan adopted by the town for applicable restrictions and
requirements.
      (2)   Where state or federal statutes impose stricter requirements, those
laws shall govern. (Refer to the town’s drinking water source protection plan
and spring source protection plan.)
   (C)   Maintenance responsibilities.
      (1)   Before town acceptance. The applicant is responsible for
maintenance of new water mains and related facilities until the town formally
accepts them by dedication.
      (2)   After town acceptance. The town shall maintain water mains and
service connections located on public property, except for service lines
between the meter and the served building, which shall be maintained by the
property owner.
      (3)   Meters. The town shall maintain all water meters, including those
on private property, and may enter private property for inspection, repair or
replacement.
   (D)   Service line connections.
      (1)   No service line connection shall be made to the town water system
without authorization from the Water Director.
      (2)   The applicant must obtain a permit, pay applicable fees and bear
the full cost of installation from the building or service location to the town
main, including trenching, piping, meter set and meter box.
      (3)   All work shall be performed by a qualified and licensed plumber or
a prequalified utility contractor, inspected and approved by the Water
Director.
      (4)   No tapping or connection to water mains is permitted when ambient
temperatures are below 40°F unless emergency exception approved by the Town
Engineer.
   (E)   Separate service lines.
      (1)   Residential lots shall have no more than one water service line per
lot unless the Planning Commission approves a second line to serve an ADU.
      (2)   Commercial or multi-tenant buildings shall have one connection with
separate service lines and meters for each unit or business.
      (3)   The town may require separation of existing shared service lines or
allow continued shared service if one party accepts responsibility for all
charges.
   (F)   Abandoned service lines. When abandoning a service line in favor of a
different service, the old line shall be disconnected and the tap plugged at
the main. All costs are the owner’s responsibility. All work must be inspected
before backfilling. Application must be filled out from the town.
   (G)   Town required relocation or replacement. If the town relocates or
replaces part of the water system, and this requires moving a customer’s
connection, the town will bear the cost of all work to replace and reconnect
the waterline.
   (H)   Unauthorized users. No customer shall allow unauthorized persons to
obtain water service from their premises.
   (I)   Water meters.
      (1)   All new service connections shall have a water meter in an
accessible location approved by the Water Director or Town Engineer. Meter
sizes set by the Town Engineer.
      (2)   Meters shall be provided and installed by the town, but only after
the main line is tested, disinfected and approved, and all fees are paid.
      (3)   Tampering with or modifying meters or meter boxes is prohibited.
      (4)   Customers are responsible for damages to town water infrastructure
on or near their premises caused by their acts or negligence, including legal
costs incurred by the town in recovering repair expenses.
   (J)   Use of unmetered water. Use of unmetered water from any service line,
main line or fire hydrant is prohibited unless authorized by the Town Council.
The use of a “jumper” in place of a meter is strictly prohibited.
   (K)   Installation before occupancy permit. All required water lines must be
installed and completed prior to issuance of occupancy permit
   (L)   Metered water use requirement.
      (1)   All water use must be metered unless otherwise authorized by the
Town Council.
         (a)   Culinary water connection. Usage is confined to properties
within town boundaries and primarily for residential or commercial buildings,
with one connection per building. If a building or structures cross over town
boundaries, it may be approved through a development agreement.
         (b)   Water permits. Issued for short-term or one time uses such as
construction, dust control or livestock watering. Livestock watering may be
permitted within and outside town boundaries, shall be metered, but shall not
include irrigation of fields or land.
      (2)   Short-term permits for construction, dust control or livestock
watering shall be limited to a maximum of 90 days and shall not establish
permanent service rights.
(Ord. 2025-15, passed 9-17-2025) Penalty, see §
50.99
§ 50.44 SPRINKLERS AND IRRIGATION SYSTEMS.
   (A)   Use of sprinklers or irrigation devices connected to the town’s
culinary water system shall not impair water pressure, fire flow or overall
system supply.
   (B)   The Town Council may, by resolution, establish restrictions on
irrigation use when necessary to protect the system. Violations shall be
subject to enforcement under §
50.99.
(Ord. 2025-15, passed 9-17-2025)
§ 50.45 APPLICATION FOR SERVICE.
   (A)   Application required. Applicants for culinary water service shall
submit a completed application on the town-approved form and shall pay all
applicable fees as established in the Town Fee Schedule.
   (B)   Agreement. Each applicant shall sign an agreement to comply with all
town ordinances, regulations and policies, and to pay all charges for service
when due.
   (C)   Deposit requirements.
      (1)   A security deposit may be required for new accounts in the amount
established in the Town Fee Schedule.
      (2)   The security deposit may be applied to any delinquent bill or
unpaid charges on the account.
      (3)   Security deposits shall be credited or refunded when service is
terminated, provided all outstanding charges have been paid in full.
      (4)   Security deposits shall also be refunded after one year of
consecutive on-time payments.
   (D)   Non-transferability.
      (1)   Service accounts are tied to the property served and shall not be
transferred to another location.
      (2)   A new application shall be required for any change in property
ownership or occupancy.
      (3)   All rates, fees and deposits shall apply to all new applications,
regardless of prior service history.
   (E)   Rates and fees.
      (1)   All rates, impact fees and service-related charges shall be
established by resolution of the Town Council in compliance with state code and
published in the Town Fee Schedule.
      (2)   Rates may vary by classification of service or customer type.
      (3)   Additional charges, including, but not limited to, late fees,
returned check fees and service disconnect/reconnect fees, shall also be
established in the Town Fee Schedule.
      (4)   All such rates and fees are enforceable as a condition of water
service.
(Ord. 2025-15, passed 9-17-2025)
§ 50.46 BILLING, NONPAYMENT, DISCONNECTION AND RECONNECTION.
   (A)   Billing and payment.
      (1)   Water meters shall be read on the last day of each month.
      (2)   Water bills shall be issued by the fifth day of each month and
shall be due on the last day of the same month.
      (3)   Payments received after the due date shall incur a late fee as
established in the Town Fee Schedule.
      (4)   Accounts not paid within 45 days past the due date shall be
considered delinquent and subject to disconnection.
   (B)   Notice of disconnect.
      (1)   Written notice shall be mailed by the town to the account holder no
fewer than five business days before the effective date of shut-off.
      (2)   A final 24-hour notice of disconnect shall be delivered to the
property before shut-off.
   (C)   Disconnection and reconnection.
      (1)   Water service may be discontinued for nonpayment or for violation
of this subchapter.
      (2)   Service shall not be restored until:
         (a)   All delinquent charges, late fees and service fees are paid in
full; and
         (b)   A new deposit is posted, if required.
   (D)   Town liability. The town shall not be liable for any damages, losses
or claims resulting from the disconnection, interruption or restoration of
water service carried out in accordance with this section.
   (E)   Returned payments. Any check or electronic payment returned unpaid by
a bank shall incur a returned payment fee as established in the Town Fee
Schedule.
   (F)   Unauthorized restoration of service. When water service has been
disconnected for nonpayment, violation of ordinance or other lawful cause, it
is unlawful for any person to restore or attempt to restore service without
authorization from the town. Violation shall be subject to enforcement under §
50.99. It is unlawful for any person to restore service without town
authorization. Violations may result in criminal penalties under the state
code.
   (G)   Use without payment prohibited. It is unlawful for any person to
obtain water from the town system without authorization or without paying for
such service. It is also unlawful to tamper with or open any valve, stopcock,
connection or fixture connected to the system without town authorization.
Violations shall constitute a Class C misdemeanor.
   (H)   Discontinuance of service.
      (1)   Customer initiated termination. 
         (a)   Any customer requesting discontinuance of service shall notify
the town in writing at least ten days before the date service is to be
terminated.
         (b)   Any credit balance resulting from advance payments or deposits
shall be refunded upon discontinuance of service.
      (2)   Town-initiated termination. The town may terminate service without
notice in emergencies or when public health and safety require.
(Ord. 2025-15, passed 9-17-2025) Penalty, see §
50.99
§ 50.47 CONFLICTS.
   If any provision of this subchapter is in conflict with a provision of
another ordinance of the town, then the most stringent requirement shall
govern.
(Ord. 2025-15, passed 9-17-2025)
§ 50.48 ENFORCEMENT.
   (A)   Tampering and unauthorized use.
      (1)   It is unlawful for any person to tamper with meters, valves,
hydrants or any part of the town’s culinary water system.
      (2)   Unauthorized connections to, or use of, the town’s water system are
strictly prohibited.
      (3)   Violations of this division (A) shall be subject to enforcement
under §
50.99; may also constitute a Class C misdemeanor under state law.
   (B)   Judicial review. Any legal action challenging a decision of the Town
Council, or any other governmental body performing a function under this
subchapter, shall be filed in a court of competent jurisdiction within 30 days
of the action being challenged.
(Ord. 2025-15, passed 9-17-2025) Penalty, see §
50.99
§ 50.99 PENALTY.
   (A)   Any person violating any provision of this chapter for which no
specific penalty is prescribed shall be subject to §
10.99.
   (B)   The town may pursue any legal or equitable remedies available under
state law to enforce compliance with §§
50.30 through
50.47, including injunctions, fines, penalties. Violations are subject to
service termination and recovery of costs and attorneys’ fees incurred in
enforcement.
(Ord. 2025-15, passed 9-17-2025)

CHAPTER 52: TELECOMMUNICATIONS
Section

§ 52.01 PURPOSE AND INTENT.
   (A)   The purpose of this chapter is to establish uniform requirements for
the granting and regulation of franchises for the installation, construction,
operation and maintenance of telecommunications systems and other utility
facilities in, on, over or under the public rights-of-way within the town.
   (B)   The town recognizes that its rights-of-way are a limited and valuable
public resource held in trust for the public and that use of these rights-of-
way must be managed to:
      (1)   Protect public safety, convenience and property;
      (2)   Ensure structural and functional integrity of the rights-of-way;
      (3)   Provide fair and reasonable compensation to the town for private
use of public property;
      (4)   Encourage competition and nondiscriminatory access among
telecommunications providers; and
      (5)   Comply with applicable state and federal laws, including the
Telecommunications Act of 1996, being Pub. Law No. 104-104, and U.C.A. § 10-8-
2.
(Prior Code, § 6.5.10)
§ 52.02 DEFINITIONS.
   For the purpose of this chapter, the following definitions shall apply
unless the context clearly indicates or requires a different meaning.
   APPLICANT. Any person or entity applying for a franchise under this chapter.
   BROADBAND. High-speed data transmission service provided over wireline or
wireless technology capable of supporting internet and related services.
   FRANCHISE. The non-exclusive right granted by the town by ordinance or
agreement to install, operate, maintain or provide a system or service within
the town rights-of-way, subject to the terms of this chapter.
   FRANCHISE AGREEMENT. A written contract between the town and a provider
authorizing use of the rights-of-way and establishing the terms of the
franchise.
   MATERIAL VIOLATION. A violation that is a serious breach of a contract that
goes to the heart of the agreement, significantly undermining its purpose and
value. Giving the non-breaching party the right to terminate the contract and
sue for damages. Examples include failing to deliver goods or services, not
completing a project or a significant violation of a non-compete clause.
   PROVIDER. Any person or entity that owns, operates or controls a system or
provides telecommunications, broadband, video or similar services using
facilities within the town’s rights-of-way.
   RIGHTS-OF-WAY (ROW). The surface and space above and below any public
street, road, highway, sidewalk, alley or easement owned or controlled by the
town for public use.
   SMALL WIRELESS FACILITY. A wireless facility meeting the size, height and
placement parameters established by the FCC and U.C.A. §§ 54-21-101 et seq.
   SYSTEM. All equipment, facilities, conduits, poles, cables, wires, fibers,
pedestals, antennas and other structures used to deliver a provider’s services.
   TELECOMMUNICATIONS SERVICES. The transmission of voice, data, graphics,
video or other information, without regard to the technology used.
(Prior Code, § 6.5.20)
§ 52.03 FRANCHISES REQUIREMENT AND GRANT OF RIGHTS.
   (A)   No provider shall construct, install, operate or maintain any system
or provide any telecommunications or utility service within the town’s rights-
of-way without first obtaining a franchise issued under this chapter.
   (B)   All franchises are non-exclusive unless otherwise approved by
ordinance.
   (C)   The franchise conveys no ownership or property interest in the rights-
of-way.
   (D)   A franchise shall be granted by ordinance and embodied in a written
franchise agreement.
   (E)   (1)   The term of any franchise shall not exceed 15 years.
      (2)   The Town Council may, by ordinance, approve one or more extensions
of a franchise; however, the total combined term of the original franchise and
any extensions shall not exceed 25 years, consistent with U.C.A. § 10-8-14.
   (F)   All franchises are subject to revocation or termination for cause as
provided herein.
   (G)   Before granting a franchise, the town shall provide notice and conduct
a public hearing consistent with U.C.A. § 10-3-710.
(Prior Code, § 6.5.30)
§ 52.04 APPLICATION AND APPROVAL PROCESS.
   (A)   Application required. A provider shall file a complete application
with the Town Recorder/Clerk on forms provided by the town, including:
      (1)   Description of the system and services to be provided;
      (2)   Proposed routes and rights-of-way usage maps;
      (3)   Proof of financial, managerial and technical capability;
      (4)   Evidence of insurance and bonding; and
      (5)   Any applicable federal or state certificates or licenses.
   (B)   Review and recommendation. The Town Engineer, Attorney and Recorder/
Clerk shall review the application for compliance and make a recommendation to
the Town Council.
   (C)   Council action. Following any required public notice and hearing under
U.C.A. § 10-3-710, the Town Council may, by ordinance, approve, approve with
conditions or deny the franchise application.
   (D)   Costs. All review and processing costs shall be borne by the applicant
as established in the Town Fee Schedule.
(Prior Code, § 6.5.40)
§ 52.05 COMPENSATION AND FEES.
   (A)   Every provider shall pay the town fair and reasonable compensation for
use of the rights-of-way, as set forth in its franchise agreement or the Town
Fee Schedule.
   (B)   Compensation may include:
      (1)   A franchise fee not to exceed the statutory maximum;
      (2)   Permit and inspection fees for construction or excavation;
      (3)   Rental or attachment fees for use of town owned poles, conduits or
structures; and
      (4)   In kind contributions such as dark fiber, service connections to
town facilities or other public benefits.
   (C)   All payments shall be remitted quarterly and accompanied by a verified
statement of gross revenues, subject to audit by the town.
   (D)   Failure to pay fees when due constitutes a material breach of the
franchise.
   (E)   Franchise fees shall not exceed the maximum percentage or amount
permitted by U.C.A. § 54-8b-2.2 and shall be applied on a nondiscriminatory
basis among similarly situated providers.
(Prior Code, § 6.5.50)
§ 52.06 CONSTRUCTION AND TECHNICAL STANDARDS.
   (A)   Providers shall comply with all applicable town, state and federal
codes, and with generally accepted engineering and safety standards.
   (B)   All facilities shall be installed and maintained so as not to endanger
public health, safety or property.
   (C)   Providers shall:
      (1)   Obtain all required construction permits before excavation or
installation;
      (2)   Restore all disturbed rights-of-way to equal or better condition;
      (3)   Coordinate work with other utilities and the town to minimize
disruption;
      (4)   Relocate or remove facilities at provider’s expense when required
for public projects; and
      (5)   Maintain accurate as-built maps of all facilities and furnish
copies to the town.
   (D)   The town may establish detailed telecommunication construction
standards by resolution, incorporated by reference into all franchise
agreements.
(Prior Code, § 6.5.60)
§ 52.07 WIRELESS AND TELECOMMUNICATIONS FACILITIES.
   (A)   Deployment of small wireless facilities, fiber optic networks and
similar telecommunications infrastructure within the rights-of-way shall comply
with this chapter and U.C.A. §§ 54-21-101 et seq.
   (B)   Providers shall obtain both a franchise and a small wireless facility
permit prior to installation.
   (C)   All wireless facilities shall:
      (1)   Be designed to minimize visual impact and preserve neighborhood
character;
      (2)   Comply with height, size and aesthetic standards adopted by the
Town Council;
      (3)   Be located on existing structures where feasible; and
      (4)   Meet all federal RF (radio frequency) emission standards.
   (D)   The town may develop additional design and location standards by
resolution consistent with federal and state law.
   (E)   The town shall process applications for small wireless facilities
within the time limits set forth in U.C.A. §§ 54-21-101 et seq. and applicable
FCC regulations.
(Prior Code, § 6.5.70)
§ 52.08 TRANSFER, ASSIGNMENT OR CHANGE OF CONTROL.
   (A)   No franchise may be transferred, assigned or sold without prior
written consent of the Town Council.
   (B)   Any proposed successor shall agree in writing to be bound by all terms
of the existing franchise.
   (C)   The provider shall notify the town in writing within 30 days of any
change in ownership or control.
   (D)   Unauthorized transfer shall be grounds for termination.
(Prior Code, § 6.5.80)
§ 52.09 INSURANCE, INDEMNIFICATION AND SECURITY.
   (A)   Each provider shall maintain insurance coverage as required by the
town, naming the town as an additional insured.
   (B)   The provider shall indemnify, defend and hold harmless the town, its
officers and employees from all claims, damages or liabilities arising from
provider’s use of the rights-of-way.
   (C)   Providers shall maintain a performance bond, letter of credit or other
security approved by the town to guarantee restoration and compliance
obligations.
(Prior Code, § 6.5.90)
§ 52.10 OVERSIGHT, RECORDS AND AUDITS.
   (A)   The town may inspect a provider’s facilities and records to ensure
compliance.
   (B)   Providers shall maintain financial and operational records for at
least three years.
   (C)   The town may conduct an audit not more than once per year;
underpayment exceeding 5% shall require reimbursement plus interest and audit
costs.
   (D)   Providers shall file an annual report summarizing construction
activity, outages and maintenance within the rights-of-way.
(Prior Code, § 6.5.100)
§ 52.11 ABANDONMENT, REVOCATION AND REMOVAL.
   (A)   Notice of discontinuance. A provider that intends to discontinue use
of any portion of its system shall notify the town in writing at least 60 days
in advance of the proposed discontinuance.
   (B)   Abandonment.
      (1)   A facility, line or portion of a system shall be deemed abandoned
if it has not been used to provide service for a continuous period of 12
months, unless the provider demonstrates to the town that the facility is still
in active use or is being maintained for future service.
      (2)   The town shall give written notice to the provider of any
facilities believed to be abandoned. The provider shall respond within 30 days
to confirm use or intent to remove.
      (3)   If the provider fails to respond, or if abandonment is confirmed,
the town may require the provider to remove the abandoned facilities at its
expense within a reasonable time not to exceed 180 days.
   (C)   Revocation of franchise. The town may revoke a franchise for any of
the following causes:
      (1)   Material violation of this chapter or the franchise agreement;
      (2)   Failure to pay required fees or compensation;
      (3)   Fraud, misrepresentation or insolvency; or
      (4)   Failure to construct or operate the system within 12 months after
the grant of the franchise, unless extended by the Town Council for good cause.
   (D)   Removal and restoration. Upon termination, revocation or abandonment,
the provider shall, at its expense, remove its facilities and restore the
affected rights-of-way to a condition equal to or better than that existing
prior to installation, as directed by the town. If the provider fails to do so,
the town may complete the removal and restoration and recover all associated
costs from the provider’s performance bond or other security.
(Prior Code, § 6.5.110)
§ 52.12 COMPLIANCE WITH LAWS.
   (A)   All franchises and providers shall comply with applicable federal,
state and town laws and regulations.
   (B)   Nothing in this chapter shall be interpreted to limit the towns’
police powers or regulatory authority under state or federal law.
   (C)   In the event of conflict, federal and state law shall control, and the
conflicting portion of this chapter shall be deemed modified to conform.
(Prior Code, § 6.5.120)

§ 70.01 ADOPTION OF UNIFORM TRAFFIC CODE.
   (A)   The town hereby adopts the most current edition of the State Traffic
Code, including the rules of the road, as compiled and published by the State
Department of Public Safety and the Utah League of Cities and Towns.
   (B)   The town further adopts by reference the Manual on Uniform Traffic
Control Devices (MUCD), as adopted and amended by UDOT, and APWA traffic
control devices and pavement markings standards, which govern fabrication,
placement and maintenance of all official signs, markings and signals within
the town.
   (C)   One copy of the adopted traffic code shall be kept on file for public
inspection in the Office of the Town Recorder/Clerk.
   (D)   The adopted code is subject to modification or supplementation by the
town ordinance.
(Prior Code, § 6.3.140)
§ 70.02 DEFINITIONS.
   For the purpose of this chapter, the following definitions shall apply
unless the context clearly indicates or requires a different meaning.
   AVERAGE DAILY TRAFFIC (ADT). The average number of vehicles that travel over
a specific road segment in a 24-hour period, including both directions of
travel for two-way roads.
   CUL-DE-SAC. A local street with only one outlet and having a turnaround for
vehicles at its terminus. CUL-DE-SACS are not permitted in the town except for
temporary access as approved.
   DIRECTOR OF ROADS. The person appointed by the town with primary
responsibility for managing the Department of Roads and overseeing the
construction, maintenance and repair of the town’s public roadways and rights-
of-way.
   ENCROACHMENT. Any unauthorized structure, improvement or obstruction placed
within a public right-of-way, easement or roadway that interferes with its
intended use.
   EXPRESSWAY. A high-speed, limited-access highway primarily used for long-
distance travel and managed by the State Department of Transportation (UDOT).
No direct access is permitted from adjoining properties.
   FENCE LINE. A barrier composed of posts, wires, rails or other materials
used as a boundary marker, which must conform to setback and visibility
standards established by the town.
   HARD SURFACE CAPPING. The use of concrete, asphalt or other durable,
approved surface materials to cover and protect a roadbed or right-of-way,
particularly where excavation or utility work has occurred.
   LOCAL AUTHORITIES. The Town Council unless otherwise defined by ordinance.
   LOCAL STREET. A road providing direct access to adjacent properties,
intended for low-speed, low-volume traffic and typically serving residential
areas.
   MAJOR ARTERIAL. A high-capacity road intended to move large volumes of
traffic between major destinations. Property access is limited and regulated.
   MASTER ROAD PLAN. The official transportation plan adopted by the town that
identifies current and future public street alignments, classifications and
rights-of-way.
   MINOR ARTERIAL. A road that provides connections between neighborhoods and
community activity centers, facilitating moderate traffic volumes with limited
access points.
   MONUMENT SIGN. A freestanding sign with a solid base mounted close to the
ground, not exceeding the height limits specified in the applicable signage
regulations.
   OBSTRUCTION. Any object-whether temporary or permanent-that impedes or
endangers travel within a public road, right-of-way or sidewalk.
   PARTIAL ROAD. A half-width roadway constructed along the boundary of a
parcel, pending future development of the adjacent parcel to complete the full
width.
   PERMITTEE. Any person or entity who has obtained written authorization from
the town to perform construction, excavation or installation activities within
the public right-of-way.
   PHANTOM ROAD. An unimproved right-of-way shown on historical or official
maps that has not been developed or opened for public use but remains under
town jurisdiction.
   PLANNING COMMISSION. The official body designated by the town to review and
make recommendations regarding land use and infrastructure matters, including
road alignments and vacations.
   PRESCRIPTIVE EASEMENT. A public or private right-of-way acquired through
continuous use over time without formal dedication or recording, as recognized
by law.
   PRIVATE ROAD. A road not dedicated to public use or maintained by the town,
generally serving commercial or HOA-managed developments and maintained under
private agreements.
   PUBLIC RIGHT-OF-WAY. Land dedicated or reserved for public use, including
streets, sidewalks, drainageways and utility corridors.
   ROADWAY LINE. The measured distance from the centerline of a road to each
edge of the platted or surveyed right-of-way.
   SIGHT DISTANCE TRIANGLE. A defined area at road intersections that must
remain clear of visual obstructions to ensure adequate visibility for motorists
and pedestrians.
   TOWN COUNCIL. The elected governing body of the town, responsible for
adopting ordinances and approving road dedications, vacations and improvements.
   UTILITY EASEMENT. A designated area within or adjacent to a road or right-
of-way reserved for the installation and maintenance of public or private
utilities.
   VEHICLE WEIGHT LIMIT. The maximum permissible weight of a vehicle (including
load) operating on town roads, typically expressed in tons per axle or total
gross vehicle weight.
   WINTER SNOW EVENT. A weather condition involving measurable snowfall that
triggers the town’s official snow removal operations and corresponding parking
restrictions.
(Prior Code, § 6.3.140)
§ 70.03 TRAFFIC REGULATIONS WITHIN TOWN LIMITS.
   (A)   Prima facie speed limits.
      (1)    Where posted, the speed limits on appropriate signs shall be the
legally enforceable maximum speed limits on those streets in accordance with
UDOT and AASHTO speed zoning criteria, based on engineering and traffic
investigation.
      (2)   Where no speed limit signs are posted, the prima facie speed limit
shall be 25 mph.
   (B)   Intersection controls. Where stop or yield signs are posted at
intersections, such designations are hereby declared official stop or yield
entrances in accordance with warrants and placement criteria in the MUTCD and
APWA guidelines.
   (C)   Angle parking.
      (1)   Where authorized by posted signs, angle parking shall be permitted
at the designated angle on the applicable streets or segments of streets to
meet AASHTO Green Book standards for maneuvering clearances.
      (2)   Posted signs shall be consistent with MUTCD and APWA guidelines.
   (D)   Traffic control posting authority.
      (1)   The Town Council in coordination with the Town Engineer or Road
Director, shall designate locations for the placement of official traffic
control devices and regulatory signs, including, but not limited to:
         (a)   Speed limit signs;
         (b)   Stop and yield signs;
         (c)   Angle parking and regulatory signs;
         (d)   Warning and guide signs; and
         (e)   Pavement markings and crosswalks.
      (2)   All devices shall comply with APWA, MUTCD and UDOT Traffic
Operations Manual requirements for sign size, retroreflectivity, placement and
maintenance.
(Prior Code, § 6.3.140)
§ 70.04 MAINTENANCE OF TRAFFIC CONTROL DEVICES.
   The Town Engineer or Director of Roads shall ensure that all signs, signals
and markings are maintained in good condition and visibility per APWA roadway
maintenance standards. Records of installation and maintenance shall be
retained in accordance with the town’s adopted recordkeeping policies.
(Prior Code, § 6.3.140)
§ 70.05 UNAUTHORIZED ENTRY AND OPERATION.
   (A)   Unauthorized entry and operation. It is unlawful for any person to
take down a fence, open a gate or enter upon the premises of another by motor
vehicle without the express or implied permission of the property owner or
lawful occupant.
   (B)   Enforcement.
      (1)   The County Sheriff’s office and the Town Director of Roads are
authorized to enforce this provision.
      (2)   Any damages to public or private property resulting from
unauthorized operation shall be subject to full restitution by the responsible
party.
   (C)   Cross-references. This section shall be read in conjunction with
U.C.A. § 41-22-10.3 (Off-Highway Vehicle Trespass) and §
70.99.
(Prior Code, § 6.3.130)
§ 70.99 PENALTY.
   (A)   Any person violating any provision of this chapter for which no
specific penalty is prescribed shall be subject to §
10.99.
   (B)   Any person who violates posted traffic regulations shall be subject to
penalties as provided under state law and any applicable town ordinances.
(Prior Code, § 6.3.140)
   (C)   Violations of §
70.05 shall constitute a Class B misdemeanor and may be enforced by citation,
impoundment or other lawful remedies available to the town.
(Prior Code, § 6.3.130)
