§ 113.01 PURPOSE AND FINDINGS.
   (A)   The purpose of this chapter is to regulate sexually oriented
businesses in a manner that promotes the health, safety, morals and general
welfare of the residents of the town. These regulations are intended to
establish reasonable and uniform standards for the operation of such
businesses.
   (B)   This chapter is not intended, nor shall it be interpreted to:
      (1)   Impose any limitation or restriction on the content of expressive
materials, including sexually oriented materials, protected by the First
Amendment to the United States Constitution;
      (2)   Deny adults access to such materials or deny distributors and
exhibitors a lawful market for their products or performances; or
      (3)   Condone or legitimize the distribution of obscene material.
   (C)   This chapter is intended to regulate the adverse secondary effects of
sexually oriented businesses, including, but not limited to, increased crime,
decreased property values and negative impacts on surrounding neighborhoods and
land uses.
(Prior Code, § 3.3.10)
§ 113.02 DEFINITIONS.
   For the purpose of this chapter, the following definitions shall apply
unless the context clearly indicates or requires a different meaning.
   ADULT ARCADE. Any place to which the public is permitted or invited in which
electronically, electrically or mechanically controlled still or motion picture
machines, projectors, video or laser disc players or other image-producing
devices, whether coin-operated, slug-operated or operated for any form of
consideration, are maintained to show images to five or fewer persons per
machine at any one time, and where the images so displayed are distinguished or
characterized by the depicting or describing of specified sexual activities or
specified anatomical areas.
   ADULT BOOKSTORE, ADULT NOVELTY STORE OR ADULT VIDEO STORE. A commercial
establishment which, as one of its principal business purposes, offers for sale
or rental, for any form of consideration, any one or more of the following:
      (1)   Books, magazines, periodicals or other printed matter, or
photographs, films, motion pictures, DVDs, video cassettes or video
reproductions, slides or other visual representations which are characterized
by the depiction or description of specified sexual activities or specified
anatomical areas; or instruments, devices or paraphernalia which are designed
or marketed for use in connection with specified sexual activities; and
      (2)   Commercial establishments may have other principal business
purposes that do not involve the offering for sale or rental of material
depicting or describing specified sexual activities or specified anatomical
areas and still be categorized as an adult bookstore, adult novelty store or
adult video store. Such other business purposes will not serve to exempt such
commercial establishments from being categorized as an adult bookstore, adult
novelty store or adult video store so long as one of its principal business
purposes is the offering for sale or rental for consideration the specified
materials which are characterized by the depiction or description of specified
sexual activities or specified anatomical areas. It shall constitute a
principal business purpose if the establishment has gross receipts of over 20%
from such materials.
   ADULT CABARET. A nightclub, bar, restaurant or similar commercial
establishment which regularly features:
      (1)   Persons who appear in a state of dress that covers no more than the
specified anatomical areas;
      (2)   Live performances or dancers whose attire covers no more than the
specified anatomical areas; or
      (3)   Films, motion pictures, videocassettes, slides or other
photographic reproductions which are characterized by the depiction or
description of specified sexual activities or specified anatomical areas.
   ADULT MOTION PICTURE THEATER.
      (1)   A commercial establishment where, for any form of consideration,
films, motion pictures, videocassettes, slides, DVDs or similar photographic
reproductions are regularly shown which are characterized by the depiction or
description of specified sexual activities or specified anatomical areas.
      (2)   A commercial establishment which:
         (a)   Excludes minors from the showing of two consecutive exhibitions
(repeated showings of any single presentation shall not be considered a
consecutive exhibition); or
         (b)   As its principal business, shows, for any form of consideration,
films, motion pictures, videocassettes, slides or similar photographic
reproductions which are primarily characterized by the depiction or description
of “specified sexual activities” or “specified anatomical areas.”
   ADULT THEATER. A theater, concert hall, auditorium or similar commercial
establishment which regularly features persons who appear in a state of dress
that covers no more than the specified anatomical areas or live performances or
dancers whose attire covers no more than the specified anatomical areas.
   EMPLOYEE. A person who performs any service on the premises of a sexually
oriented business on a full-time, part-time or contract basis, whether or not
the person is denominated an employee, independent contractor, agent or
otherwise and whether or not the person is paid a salary, wage or other
compensation by the operator of the business. EMPLOYEE does not include a
person exclusively on the premises for repair or maintenance of the premises or
equipment on the premises or for the delivery of goods to the premises.
   ESCORT. Any person who, for compensation, offers companionship or social
interaction that may be reasonably interpreted as intended to provide sexual
stimulation or gratification.
   ESCORT AGENCY. A business that furnishes or offers to furnish escorts for a
fee, commission, hire or other consideration.
   ESTABLISHMENT. Includes any of the following:
      (1)   The opening or commencement of any sexually oriented business as a
new business;
      (2)   The conversion of an existing business, whether or not a sexually
oriented business, to any sexually oriented business;
      (3)   The addition of any sexually oriented business to any other
existing sexually oriented business; or
      (4)   The relocation of any sexually oriented business.
   LICENSEE. A person in whose name a license to operate a sexually oriented
business has been issued, as well as the individual listed as an applicant on
the application for a license; and in the case of an employee, a person in
whose name a license has been issued authorizing employment in a sexually
oriented business.
   MANAGER’S STATION. A designated area within a sexually oriented business
where a licensed employee is assigned to monitor patron activity and ensure
compliance with applicable laws and regulations. A MANAGER’S STATION shall not
exceed 32 square feet in floor area.
   MINOR. Any person under the age of 18 years.
   PATRON ACCESS AREA. Any area within the premises of a sexually oriented
business where a customer or member of the public is permitted.
   SEXUALLY ORIENTED BUSINESS. Any business that engages in the offering of
services, performances or materials that are distinguished or characterized by
an emphasis on specified sexual activities or specified anatomical areas,
including, but not limited to, adult arcades, adult bookstores, adult video
stores, adult cabarets, adult motels, adult motion picture theaters, nude
modeling studios, sexual encounter centers and escort agencies.
   SEXUALLY ORIENTED BUSINESS EMPLOYEE. Any person employed by a sexually
oriented business who provides services or performs work on the premises,
whether full-time, part-time, permanent or temporary, including managers,
entertainers, escorts and other support staff.
   SPECIFIED ANATOMICAL AREAS.
      (1)   Less than completely and opaquely covered human genitals, pubic
region, buttocks, anus or female breasts below a point immediately above the
top of the areola; or
      (2)   Human male genitals in a discernibly turgid state, even if
completely and opaquely covered.
   SPECIFIED CRIMINAL ACTIVITY. Any offense, regardless of title, involving the
following:
      (1)   Prostitution or promotion of prostitution; dissemination of
obscenity; sale, distribution or display of harmful material to a minor; sexual
performance by a child; possession or distribution of child pornography; public
lewdness; indecent exposure; indecency with a child; engaging in organized
criminal activity; sexual assault; molestation of a child; gambling;
distribution of a controlled substance; or any similar offenses to those
described above under the criminal or penal code of other states or countries;
for which:
         (a)   Less than three years have elapsed since the date of conviction
or the date of release from confinement imposed for the conviction, whichever
is the later date, if the conviction is of a misdemeanor offense;
         (b)   Less than five years have elapsed since the date of conviction
or the date of release from confinement for the conviction, whichever is the
later date, if the conviction is of a felony offense; or
         (c)   Less than five years have elapsed since the date of the last
conviction or the date of release from confinement for the last conviction,
whichever is the later date, if the convictions are of two or more misdemeanor
offenses or combination of misdemeanor offenses occurring within any 36-month
period.
      (2)   That a conviction is being appealed shall have no effect on the
disqualification of the applicant or a person residing with the applicant.
   SPECIFIED SEXUAL ACTIVITIES. Includes any of the following:
      (1)   Human genitals in a state of sexual stimulation or arousal;
      (2)   Acts of human masturbation, sexual intercourse, sodomy, oral
copulation or bestiality;
      (3)   Fondling or other erotic touching of human genitals, pubic region,
buttocks, anus or female breasts; and
      (4)   Excretory functions as part of or in connection with any of the
activities set forth above.
   SUBSTANTIAL ENLARGEMENT OF A SEXUALLY ORIENTED BUSINESS. The increase in
inventory or floor areas occupied by the business by more than 10%, as the
floor areas exist on the date the ordinance codified in this chapter takes
effect.
   TOWN. Fairfield, Utah.
   TRANSFER OF OWNERSHIP OR CONTROL OF A SEXUALLY ORIENTED BUSINESS. Includes
any of the following:
      (1)   The sale, lease or sublease of the business;
      (2)   The transfer of securities which constitute a controlling interest
in the business, whether by sale, exchange or similar means; or
      (3)   The establishment of a trust, gift or other similar legal device
which transfers the ownership or control of the business, including transfer by
bequest or other operation of law, upon the death of the person possessing the
ownership or control.
   VIEWING ROOM OR BOOTH. An enclosed or partitioned area within a sexually
oriented business where a person may view films, video recordings or similar
visual representations depicting specified sexual activities or specified
anatomical areas.
(Prior Code, § 3.3.20)
§ 113.03 CLASSIFICATION OF BUSINESSES.
   Sexually oriented businesses are classified into the following categories:
   (A)   Adult arcades;
   (B)   Adult bookstores, adult novelty stores or adult video stores;
   (C)   Adult cabarets;
   (D)   Adult motion picture theaters;
   (E)   Adult theaters; and
   (F)   Escort agencies.
(Prior Code, § 3.3.30)
§ 113.04 LICENSE REQUIRED.
   (A)   It is unlawful:
      (1)   For any person to operate a sexually oriented business without a
valid sexually oriented business license issued by the town;
      (2)   For any sexually oriented business to employ a person who does not
possess a valid sexually oriented business employee license issued by the town;
or
      (3)   For any person to obtain employment at a sexually oriented business
without securing a valid sexually oriented business employee license from the
town.
   (B)   License application requirements are as follows.
      (1)   All applicants shall complete an official town application form.
      (2)   No sexually oriented business shall operate within 2,500 feet of a
church, school, park, residential or another sexually oriented business.
      (3)   Viewing booths in sexually oriented businesses shall be constructed
in accordance with town building and fire codes to prevent unauthorized
activities.
      (4)   Applications shall include fingerprints, proof of identity and any
other necessary documentation as determined by the town.
      (5)   If the applicant is a business entity, all owners, partners,
members of an LLC or any other type of organization, with at least a 20%
interest in the sexually oriented business must provide identifying
information, be listed as applicants and sign the application. Each applicant
must be qualified as an applicant and shall be considered a licensee if a
license is granted.
      (6)   The applicant(s) must disclose all prior denials, suspensions or
revocations of similar licenses and any prior convictions of specified criminal
activity.
      (7)   A detailed site plan, drawn to scale, must be submitted for
approval.
      (8)   If the applicant does not own the business premises, a signed
letter from the property owner acknowledging the intended business use must be
provided.
      (9)   A background security check shall be conducted at the expense of
the applicant.
      (10)   Employees shall submit to fingerprinting and provide recent
photographs with their application.
      (11)   Additional requirements include:
         (a)   Compliance with the ordinance and application requirements;
         (b)   The absence of criminal disqualifications;
         (c)   Adherence to zoning and land use restrictions;
         (d)   The single classification of license for which the applicant is
filing; and
         (e)   Location of a proposed sexually oriented business, with legal
description, street address, town and telephone number.
   (C)   The completed application for a sexually oriented business license
shall contain the following information and shall be accompanied by the
following documents:
      (1)   If the applicant is:
         (a)   An individual, the individual shall state his or her legal name
and any aliases and submit proof that he or she is a minimum of 18 years of
age;
         (b)   A partnership, the partnership shall state its complete name and
the names of all general partners, whether the partnership is general or
limited; if it is a limited partnership, the principal limited partners legally
or equitably holding 20% or more of any class of interest or of the voting,
capital or income interests in the limited partnership, the name of the
registered agent and the address of the registered office for service of
process and a copy of the partnership agreement, if any;
         (c)   A corporation, the corporation shall state its complete name,
the date of its incorporation, evidence that the corporation is in good
standing under the laws of its state of incorporation, the names and capacity
of all officers, directors and principal stockholders legally or equitably
holding 20% or more of any class of stock or of the voting rights in the
corporation and the name of the registered corporate agent and the address of
the registered office for service of process;
         (d)   A limited liability company, the company shall state its
complete name, the date of its organization, evidence that the company is in
good standing under the laws of its state of organization, the names and
capacity of all members with management authority, managers, officers,
directors and principal members legally or equitably holding 20% or more of any
class of interest or of the voting, capital or income interests in the company
and the name of the registered agent and the address of the registered office
for service of process; or
         (e)   If the applicant is any other form of unincorporated
organization, the organization shall state its type of organization, its state
of organization, complete name, the names of all associates, members or if
there are more than 100 of them, principal associates or members legally or
equitably holding 20% or more of any class of interest or of the voting,
capital or income interests in the organization, the names and capacity of all
associates or members with management authority, managers, officers, directors
and fiduciaries and the name of the registered agent and the address of the
registered office for service of process and a copy of any organizational
documents.
      (2)   If the applicant intends to operate the sexually oriented business
under a name other than that of the applicant, he or she must state the
sexually oriented business’s fictitious name and submit the required
registration documents;
      (3)   Whether the applicant, or a person residing with the applicant, has
been convicted of a specified criminal activity as defined in this chapter,
and, if so, the specified criminal activity involved, the date, place and
jurisdiction of each;
      (4)   Whether the applicant, or a person residing with the applicant, or
any person described in division (C)(1) above with respect to the applicant,
has had a previous license under this title, or other similar sexually oriented
business ordinances from another town or county, denied, suspended or revoked,
including the name and location of the sexually oriented business for which the
permit was denied, suspended or revoked, as well as the date of the denial,
suspension or revocation and whether the applicant or a person residing with
the applicant or any person described in division (C)(1) above with respect to
the applicant, has been:
         (a)   A general partner or principal limited partner in a partnership;
         (b)   An officer, director or principal stockholder of a corporation;
         (c)   A manager, member with management authority, officer or
principal member of a limited liability company; or
         (d)   An officer, director, fiduciary, associate or member with
management authority, manager or principal associate or manager of any other
unincorporated organization, that is or was licensed under this title whose
license has previously been denied, suspended or revoked, including the name
and location of the sexually oriented business for which the permit was denied,
suspended or revoked as well as the date of the denial, suspension or
revocation.
      (5)   Whether the applicant, or a person residing with the applicant or
any person described in division (C)(1) above with respect to the applicant,
holds any other licenses under this title or other similar sexually oriented
business ordinance from another town or county and, if so, the names and
locations of such other licensed businesses;
      (6)   The single classification of license for which the applicant is
filing;
      (7)   The location of a proposed sexually oriented business, including a
legal description of the property, street address, town and telephone number
(s), if any;
      (8)   The applicant’s mailing address and residential address and this
same information with respect to any person described in division (C)(1) above
with respect to the applicant;
      (9)   A recent photograph of the applicant(s) (if individuals) and of any
persons described in division (C)(1) above with respect to the applicant;
      (10)   The applicant’s driver’s license number, Social Security number
and state or federally issued tax or employer identification numbers, and this
same information with respect to any person described in division (C)(1) above
with respect to the applicant;
      (11)   A sketch or diagram showing the configuration of the premises,
including a statement of total floor space occupied by the business. The sketch
or diagram need not be professionally prepared, but it must be drawn to a
designated scale or drawn with marked dimensions of the interior of the
premises to an accuracy of plus or minus six inches;
      (12)   A current certificate and straight-line drawing prepared within 30
days prior to application by a registered land surveyor depicting the proper
lines and the structures containing any existing sexually oriented businesses
within 2,500 feet of the property to be certified; the property lines of any
established church, religious institution or synagogue, school or public park
or recreation area within 2,500 feet of the property to be certified. For the
purpose of this section, a use shall be considered existing or established if
it is in existence at the time an application is submitted;
      (13)   If an applicant wishes to operate a sexually oriented business,
which shall exhibit on the premises, in a viewing room or booth of less than
150 square feet of floor space, films, videocassettes, other video
reproductions or live entertainment which depict specified sexual activities or
specified anatomical areas, then the applicant shall comply with the
application requirements set forth in §
113.13; and
      (14)   If the property on which the sexually oriented business is to be
located is owned by any person or entity other than the applicant, the
applicant shall submit a letter, signed by the owner, stating that the
applicant has fully disclosed to the owner that the business to be operated is
a sexually oriented business, and that the type and nature of the inventory has
also been disclosed.
   (D)   Before any applicant may be issued a sexually oriented business
employee license, the applicant shall submit on a form, to be provided by the
town licensing official the following information:
      (1)   The applicant’s name or any other name (including “stage” names) or
aliases used by the individual;
      (2)   Age, date and place of birth;
      (3)   Height, weight, hair and eye color;
      (4)   Present residence address and telephone number;
      (5)   Present business address and telephone number;
      (6)   Date, issuing state and number of driver’s permit or other
identification card information;
      (7)   Social Security number;
      (8)   Proof that the individual is at least 18 years of age; and
      (9)   A background security check with the application, for all
individuals listed on the application (fees paid for by applicants).
   (E)   Attached to the application form for a sexually oriented business
employee license, as provided above, shall be the following:
      (1)   A color photograph of the applicant clearly showing the applicant’s
face, and the applicant’s fingerprints on a form provided by the Police
Department. Any fees for the photographs and fingerprints shall be paid by the
applicant;
      (2)   A statement detailing the license history of the applicant for the
five years immediately preceding the date of the filing of the application,
including whether such applicant previously operated or is seeking to operate,
in this or any other county, city, state or country, any other sexually
oriented business, has ever had a license, permit or authorization to do
business denied, revoked or suspended, or had any professional or vocational
license or permit denied, revoked or suspended. In the event of any such
denial, revocation or suspension, state the name, the name of the issuing or
denying jurisdiction, and describe in full the reason for the denial,
revocation or suspension. A copy of any order of denial, revocation or
suspension shall be attached to the application; and
      (3)   A statement whether the applicant has been convicted of a specified
criminal activity and, if so, the specified criminal activity involved, the
date, place and jurisdiction of each.
(Prior Code, § 3.3.40) Penalty, see §
113.99
§ 113.05 ISSUANCE OF LICENSE.
   (A)   Employee license application and issuance.
      (1)   Upon submission of a complete application for a sexually oriented
business employee license, the application shall be reviewed by the appropriate
town departments. The application process shall be completed within 30 days of
submission.
      (2)   A license shall be issued unless a preponderance of the evidence
establishes that one or more of the following conditions exist:
         (a)   The applicant provided incomplete or false information on the
application;
         (b)   The applicant is under 18 years of age;
         (c)   The applicant has been convicted of a specified criminal
activity as defined in this chapter;
         (d)   The license is intended for employment in a business prohibited
by local, state or federal law; and
         (e)   The applicant has had a sexually oriented business employee
license revoked by the town within the past three years, or within five years
if revoked due to a criminal conviction.
      (3)   Denial, suspension or revocation of a license may be appealed as
outlined in this chapter.
   (B)   Sexually oriented business license application and issuance. The town
shall process a completed sexually oriented business license application within
30 days. A license shall be granted unless a preponderance of the evidence
establishes that one or more of the following conditions exist:
      (1)   The applicant is under 18 years of age;
      (2)   The applicant or an individual residing with the applicant has
outstanding taxes, fees, fines or penalties owed to the town;
      (3)   The applicant provided incomplete or false information on the
application;
      (4)   The applicant or an individual residing with the applicant has been
denied a sexually oriented business license or had one revoked within the past
12 months;
      (5)   The applicant or an individual residing with the applicant has been
convicted of a specified criminal activity;
      (6)   The business premises fail to meet health, fire, building or zoning
codes;
      (7)   The required license fee has not been paid; and/or
      (8)   The applicant is not in compliance with applicable town or state
laws.
   (C)   License renewals. Licenses must be renewed annually upon:
      (1)   Application and verification that the licensee remains in
compliance with all licensing requirements;
      (2)   Verification that applicant has not been convicted of any specified
criminal activity or committed any act during the existence of the previous
license which would be grounds to deny the initial license application; and
      (3)   Renewal requires payment of the all applicable fees.
   (D)   License display requirements. Business licenses shall:
      (1)   State the name of the licensee, expiration date, business address
and business classification pursuant to §
113.03;
      (2)   Shall be issued for only one classification pursuant to §
113.03; and
      (3)   Be posted in a conspicuous location at or near the business
entrance.
   (E)   Location restrictions.
      (1)   Sexually oriented businesses may not be established within 2,500
feet of a residence, school, church, library, playground or park.
      (2)   Distance shall be measured by the shortest pedestrian or vehicular
route from the business entrance to the nearest restricted facility boundary.
   (F)   License revocation and disqualification.
      (1)   A license may be revoked if a licensee or relevant individual is
convicted of specified criminal activity.
      (2)   The town may suspend a license upon arrest of a relevant individual
for specified criminal activity pending adjudication.
      (3)   Licensees must report any changes in business ownership or
management to the town immediately.
      (4)   If any relevant individual has a prior license revoked within the
past three years, the applicant is ineligible for licensure.
      (5)   If any applicant or relevant person is convicted of specified
criminal activity subsequent to the issuance of the license, the license shall
be surrendered immediately. The licensee may request a hearing on the matter,
in writing and within ten days of a conviction by a trial court. Any such
hearing shall be pursuant to the provisions of Chapter 110. If a licensee no
longer meets the qualifications required by this chapter, the town may suspend
or revoke the license.
(Prior Code, § 3.3.50) Penalty, see §
113.99
§ 113.06 FEES.
   (A)   All applications for a sexually oriented business license, whether new
or for renewal, must include a non-refundable application investigation fee, as
outlined in the Town Fee Schedule.
   (B)   In addition to the application and investigation fee, all sexually
oriented businesses granted a license, either new or renewed, must pay an
annual license fee, as specified in the Town Fee Schedule. This fee must be
paid within 30 days of license issuance or renewal.
   (C)   All license applications and fees must be submitted to the Town
Licensing Official.
   (D)   The fees required under this section are in addition to any other
applicable fees outlined in this title.
(Prior Code, § 3.3.60)
§ 113.07 INSPECTION.
   (A)   The applicant or licensee must allow representatives from the Police
Department, Health Department, Fire Department, Licensing Office or any other
relevant town departments or agencies, including officials contracted to
provide these services, to inspect the premises of a sexually oriented
business. Inspections may occur at any time the business is occupied or open
for operation to ensure compliance with applicable laws and regulations during
normal business hours or while the premises are occupied.
   (B)   It is a Class B misdemeanor for any owner, agent or employee of a
sexually oriented business to refuse a lawful inspection of the premises during
business hours or while the premises are occupied.
(Prior Code, § 3.3.70) Penalty, see §
113.99
§ 113.08 EXPIRATION OF LICENSE.
   (A)   All licenses issued under this chapter shall expire concurrently with
other business licenses as outlined in Chapter 110. Renewal applications must
be submitted at least 30 days before the license expiration date. If a renewal
application is submitted less than 30 days before expiration, the existing
license will remain valid until the town processes the renewal.
   (B)   If the town denies a license renewal, the applicant shall be
ineligible for a new license for one year from the date of denial. However, if
the reason for denial has been corrected or resolved, the applicant may reapply
for a license after 90 days from the date the denial became final.
(Prior Code, § 3.3.80)
§ 113.09 SUSPENSION OF LICENSE.
   The town shall suspend a license for a period of no less than ten days and
no more than 30 days if it determines that the licensee or an employee of the
licensee has:
   (A)   Violated any provision of this title, failed to comply with applicable
regulations, or is no longer eligible for the license under §
113.05; or
   (B)   Refused to allow an authorized inspection of the sexually oriented
business premises as required by this chapter.
(Prior Code, § 3.3.90) Penalty, see §
113.99
§ 113.10 REVOKING A LICENSE.
   (A)   Mandatory revocation due to prior suspension. The town shall revoke a
sexually oriented business license if any cause for suspension, as outlined in
§
113.09, occurs and the license has been suspended within the preceding 12
months.
   (B)   Grounds for revocation revoking a license. The town shall revoke a
license if it determines that any of the following have occurred:
      (1)   The licensee submitted false or misleading information as part of
the application process;
      (2)   A legally defined minor was allowed to enter the premises under any
circumstances;
      (3)   The licensee knew or reasonably should have known that controlled
substances were possessed, used or sold on the premises;
      (4)   The licensee knew or reasonably should have known that acts of
prostitution occurred on the premises;
      (5)   The licensee knew or reasonably should have known that the business
operated while the license was under suspension;
      (6)   The licensee knew or reasonably should have known, that sexual acts
including intercourse, sodomy, oral copulation, masturbation or similar conduct
occurred on the premises;
      (7)   The licensee knew or reasonably should have known that obscene
materials, child pornography or other contraband were present on the premises;
      (8)   The licensee is delinquent in payment of any taxes or fees owed to
the town, county or state; and
      (9)   The licensee is no longer eligible for a license under the
provisions of §
113.05.
   (C)   Duration and conditions of revocation for revoking a license.
      (1)   A license revocation shall remain in effect for one year from the
date it becomes effective.
      (2)   During this period, the licensee shall not be eligible to receive a
new sexually oriented business license.
      (3)   After at least 90 days from the effective date of the revocation,
the town may consider a new application if it finds substantial mitigating
circumstances or corrective measures have been taken:
         (a)   Example of mitigating circumstances. The misconduct was caused
by an employee or customer acting against the licensee’s instructions; or
         (b)   Example of corrective measures. Termination of the offending
employee or barring the offending patron from the premises.
   (D)   Permanent disqualification. A licensee whose license has been revoked
three times within any five-year period shall be permanently disqualified from
obtaining a sexually oriented business license from the town.
   (E)   Appeals.
      (1)   A licensee or applicant may appeal the denial, suspension or
revocation of a license to the Town Council.
      (2)   The appeal must be submitted in writing to the town’s licensing
official within ten days of the decision.
      (3)   The Town Council may either review the decision on the record or
hold a hearing as outlined in §
113.14.
      (4)   The Council may affirm, reverse or modify the decision and shall
issue a written determination within 30 days of receiving the appeal.
      (5)   Further appeals shall be made to the appropriate district court.
      (6)   Unless an injunction or writ of mandamus is issued by the court,
the status quo ante shall be maintained during the appeal process. Additional
enforcement actions may still proceed.
(Prior Code, § 3.3.100)
§ 113.11 TRANSFER OF LICENSE PROHIBITED.
   (A)   A sexually oriented business license is non-transferable.
   (B)   A licensee shall not:
      (1)   Transfer or assign the license to another person or entity; or
      (2)   Operate the sexually oriented business at any location other than
the address specified in the approved license application.
(Prior Code, § 3.3.110) Penalty, see §
113.99
§ 113.12 LOCATION OF SEXUALLY ORIENTED BUSINESSES.
   It is a Class C misdemeanor for any person to operate, or cause to be
operated, a sexually oriented business in any zoning district where such use is
not expressly permitted by the town’s zoning regulations. For zoning location
compatibility, please refer to Title 15, Land Usage.
(Prior Code, § 3.3.120) Penalty, see §
113.99
§ 113.13 REGULATIONS FOR VIEWING ROOMS EXHIBITING SEXUALLY EXPLICIT MATERIAL.
   Any person who operates, or causes to be operated, a sexually oriented
business that exhibits films, video recordings or other visual media depicting
specified sexual activities or specified anatomical areas in viewing rooms of
less than 150 square feet must comply with the following requirements.
   (A)   Premises diagram required. A diagram of the premises must be submitted
with the license application. The diagram shall:
      (1)   Indicate the location of all manager’s stations;
      (2)   Show all overhead lighting fixtures;
      (3)   Designate all areas where patrons are prohibited;
      (4)   Identify the location where the business license will be
conspicuously posted, if approved;
      (5)   Manager’s stations shall not exceed 32 square feet in floor area;
      (6)   The diagram does not need to be professionally drafted but must:
         (a)   Be oriented to the north or to a designated landmark or street;
and
         (b)   Be drawn to scale or include marked dimensions accurate to
within six inches.
      (7)   The town may waive this requirement for renewal applications if the
applicant certifies that no changes have been made to the previously submitted
and approved layout.
   (B)   Manager’s station and supervision requirements.
      (1)   The application must be sworn to be true and accurate.
      (2)   No changes to the location or configuration of manager’s stations
may be made without prior approval from the town.
      (3)   The licensee must ensure that at least one licensed employee is on
duty and present in each designated manager’s station whenever any patron is
inside the premises;
   (C)   Visibility and monitoring.
      (1)   The interior layout must allow an unobstructed line of sight from
at least one manager’s station to every area accessible to patrons, excluding
restrooms.
      (2)   If more than one manager’s station is designated, the configuration
must provide full visibility of all patron-accessible areas from at least one
station. The view required must be a direct line of sight from the manager’s
station.
      (3)   Restrooms shall not:
         (a)   Contain any video display equipment; and
         (b)   Permit video viewing from within.
   (D)   Obstruction prohibited. The licensee must:
      (1)   Ensure that no doors, curtains, partitions, walls, merchandise,
racks or other items obstruct any required view areas; and
      (2)   Prevent patron access to any portion of the premises that was
designated in the submitted diagram as off-limits.
   (E)   Viewing room standards.
      (1)   Only one person may occupy a viewing room or booth at a time.
      (2)   Overhead lighting must:
         (a)   Provide at least five foot-candles of illumination at floor
level in all patron-accessible areas.
         (b)   Be maintained at this level whenever patrons are present.
      (3)   No openings of any kind may exist between viewing rooms or booths.
      (4)   Patrons are prohibited from creating or attempting to create any
openings between viewing booths.
      (5)   The licensee shall inspect viewing room walls daily to ensure no
holes or openings exist.
      (6)   Floor coverings in viewing rooms must be:
         (a)   Nonporous and easily cleanable; and
         (b)   Free of rugs or carpeting.
      (7)   Walls, floors and ceilings within 48 inches of the floor must be:
         (a)   Made of or permanently covered with nonporous, easily cleanable
material; and
         (b)   Free from wood, plywood, composition board or other porous
surfaces.
      (8)   Failure to comply with any requirement in this section by a person
responsible under this section is a Class B misdemeanor.
(Prior Code, § 3.3.130) Penalty, see §
113.99
§ 113.14 ADDITIONAL REGULATIONS FOR ESCORT AGENCIES.
   Escort agencies and their employees are subject to the following
regulations.
   (A)   Employment of minors prohibited. An escort agency shall not employ any
individual under the age of 18 years.
   (B)   Providing escort services to minors prohibited. It is unlawful for any
person to act as, or agree to act as, an escort for a person under the age of
18 years.
   (C)   Prohibited activities on agency premises. No escort shall perform any
escort-related activity or service on the premises of the escort agency.
   (D)   Off-premises conduct restrictions. In addition to the restrictions
listed in §
113.10, all such restrictions apply to the conduct of any escort agency
employee during the time escort services are being provided, regardless of
location.
(Prior Code, § 3.3.140) Penalty, see §
113.99
§ 113.15 ADDITIONAL REGULATIONS CONCERNING LICENSEE EMPLOYEES.
   It is unlawful for any licensee employee to engage in physical contact with
any other person while performing their employment duties.
(Prior Code, § 3.3.150) Penalty, see §
113.99
§ 113.16 PROHIBITION AGAINST MINORS IN SEXUALLY ORIENTED BUSINESSES.
   (A)   It is a misdemeanor for any person to knowingly or negligently allow
an individual under the age of 18 years to enter or remain on the premises of a
sexually oriented business.
   (B)   Licensees have an affirmative duty to verify the age of all persons on
the premises and to ensure that no individuals under the age of 18 are
permitted access at any time.
(Prior Code, § 3.3.160) Penalty, see §
113.99
§ 113.17 HOURS OF OPERATION.
   No sexually oriented business shall operate or be open to the public between
the hours of 1:00 a.m. and 1:00 p.m.
(Prior Code, § 3.3.170) Penalty, see §
113.99
§ 113.99 PENALTY.
   (A)   Any person who operates, or causes to be operated, a sexually oriented
business without a valid license, or in violation of any provision of this
chapter, may be subject to:
      (1)   A civil action for injunctive relief; and
      (2)   Criminal prosecution.
   (B)   Each day a sexually oriented business operates in violation of this
chapter constitutes a separate offense.
   (C)   A violation of this chapter is classified as a Class B misdemeanor and
is punishable according to applicable state law.
   (D)   Violations of this chapter shall be subject to:
      (1)   Fines as established by the Town Council;
      (2)   Suspension or revocation of the business or employee license; and
      (3)   Additional penalties as authorized by law.
(Prior Code, § 3.3.180)

**** GROWTH MANAGEMENT ****
§ 150.01 FINDINGS.
   The people of the town find and declare as follows.
   (A)   The town has adopted ordinances and a general plan relating to the
regulation for residential development.
   (B)   The town is experiencing a period of residential development which is
adversely affecting the capacity of the streets to meet traffic demands, the
capacity to provide fire services and water, the capacity of the area school to
absorb children in an orderly way, the historic character of the community, the
quality of life which had characterized this community and the cost to
households for utilities and municipal services.
   (C)   It is the intent of the people of the community to achieve a steady
rate of residential growth each year rather than a fluctuating, overly rapid
rate in order that the services provided by the town and area schools, parks,
utilities and service agencies operating in the town and the surrounding region
can be properly and effectively staged in a manner which will not overextend
existing facilities, and in order to bring existing services up to necessary
standards while minimizing the avoidable cost of short-sighted facility
expansion, by means of long-term planning.
   (D)   It is the intent of the people of the town to establish control over
quality, distribution and rate of growth of the town in the interest of:
      (1)   Preserving the character of the community;
      (2)   Protecting the open space of the community;
      (3)   Protecting the quality of life in the town;
      (4)   Ensuring the adequacy of town facilities, school facilities,
recreation and park facilities and services;
      (5)   Ensuring the adequacy of fire protection; and
      (6)   Ensuring an adequate water supply for current and future residents.
   (E)   It is the purpose of this subchapter to augment the policies of the
town as recorded in the general plan and other town ordinances relating to
regulating development.
   (F)   In order to facilitate the purposes, the town must be able to control
the rate, distribution, quality and economic level of the proposed development.
Control systems for the town codified in this subchapter shall be in effect
after the effective date of the ordinance codified in this subchapter until
amended.
   (G)   It is furthermore the intent of the people of the town that the
awarding of building permit allotments pursuant to this subchapter be
accomplished, in accordance with the criteria set forth herein, fairly,
impartially and without discrimination against any particular parcel of land,
development project or developer.
   (H)   This subchapter shall regulate the time or rate of development based
on existing zoning or other land use approvals applying to a particular parcel
of land or development.
(Prior Code, § 9.5.10)
§ 150.02 APPLICABILITY OF THE DEVELOPMENT CONTROL SYSTEM.
   The system set out in this subchapter shall apply from the effective date of
the ordinance codified in this subchapter. This subchapter shall apply to all
residential development in the town, including single-family residential units
on a single existing lot, but not the rehabilitation or remodeling of an
existing dwelling.
(Prior Code, § 9.5.20)
§ 150.03 ADMINISTRATION.
   The Planning Commission shall administer the system set forth in this
subchapter.
(Prior Code, § 9.5.30)
§ 150.04 ANNUAL BUILDING PERMIT PERCENTAGE ESTABLISHED.
   (A)   The number of new residential building permits issued each year in the
town will be a maximum of 10% of the existing dwellings within the town.
   (B)   The annual allotment shall be continuously applicable to the town’s
jurisdictional boundaries and shall include any additional territory annexed.
   (C)   For the purposes of this subchapter, a YEAR shall be the calendar
year. If the annual allotment of building permits for a given year is not
allotted, it cannot be carried over to a subsequent year.
(Prior Code, § 9.5.40)
§ 150.05 BUILDING PERMIT APPLICATION.
   (A)   The owner/builder of proposed projects may apply for a building permit
as set forth, and as in other town ordinances.
   (B)   The Building Department shall examine each application for its
relation to or impact upon local public facilities and services and shall
evaluate each development or lot on the criteria set forth below:
      (1)   The capacity of the water system to provide for the needs of the
proposed development must comply with
Chapter 50 of this code;
      (2)   The capacity of the drainage facilities to adequately dispose of
the surface runoff of the proposed development;
      (3)   The ability of the Fire Department to provide fire protection
according to the established response standards of the town without the
necessity of requiring additional major equipment or housing facilities;
      (4)   How the site and architectural design quality may be adversely
affected by modification to topography, grading, cut or fill of natural slopes
and weather;
      (5)   How the proposed buildings and related construction will visually
disturb ridge lines and natural community vistas;
      (6)   The absence of deleterious impact on farmland; and
      (7)   The absence of deleterious impact on historical or cultural
landmarks.
(Prior Code, § 9.5.50)
§ 150.06 BUILDING PERMIT EVALUATIONS.
   (A)   The Planning Commission shall approve building permits on a “first
come first served” basis until all available permits are issued each year in
accordance with this subchapter. This assumes that the applicants have
satisfied all of the criteria of this and the other applicable town ordinances,
including, but not limited to, zoning and water ordinances. Incomplete or
erroneous applications will be returned to the applicant and be removed from
consideration until returned totally complete.
   (B)   A building permit must be obtained (and fees paid) within 60 days of
the plan review approval of the building permit application by the Planning
Commission.
   (C)   Building permit applications will only be accepted on or after the
first day of each calendar year for permits allocated in that year.
   (D)   A $1,500 cashier’s check made out to the town is required as a deposit
at the time of submission of a building permit application package. If the
$1,500 deposit was paid to reserve a building permit allotment for that given
year, that deposit can be transferred to the building permit application fee.
This total deposit fee will be deducted from the approved building permit cost
at the time all the fees are paid for the entire cost of the approved building
permit. All fees, including impact fees, must be paid in full in order to
obtain an approved building permit. If for any reason a building permit cannot
be obtained after the application deposit was made, the deposit fee will not be
returned.
   (E)   Building permits are issued in order of applications received with a
paid, non-refundable application fee.
(Prior Code, § 9.5.60)
§ 150.07 DEVELOPMENT ALLOTMENT AWARDS.
   (A)   The number of dwelling units for which development allotments can be
issued shall not exceed the number established in §
150.04 of this chapter.
   (B)   No single developer shall, in any one year, be issued development
allotments for dwelling units except as submitted as individual requests.
   (C)   Should an applicant fail to initiate construction within 12 months
after award of the building permit allotment, the Planning Commission will
rescind the allotment.
(Prior Code, § 9.5.70)
**** RIGHT TO FARM ****
§ 150.20 PURPOSE.
   The town values its rich agricultural heritage and considers agricultural
uses as a component of the town’s community fabric and quality of life
amenities and contributions to the town’s economic base. The town places great
importance on its agricultural areas and the protection and preservation of
agricultural land and agricultural activities within the town.
(Prior Code, § 9.7.10)
§ 150.21 DEFINITIONS.
   For the purpose of this subchapter, the following definitions shall apply
unless the context clearly indicates or requires a different meaning.
   AGRICULTURAL AREA. Land actively used or zoned for the cultivation of crops,
raising of livestock, orchards, pastures or other agricultural production,
including land historically used for such purposes.
   AGRICULTURAL DISCLOSURE NOTE. A required statement placed on a recorded
subdivision plat that notifies future property owners of the presence and
normal operations of nearby agricultural activities, including noise, odors,
pests and livestock.
   AGRICULTURAL FENCE (NON-CLIMB). A type of barrier commonly used for
containing or excluding livestock, constructed with vertical mesh openings no
larger than two inches by four inches and designed to prevent animals or people
from climbing or passing through. Required specifications include steel posts,
top rails and durable fastening systems.
   AGRICULTURAL LAND. Any parcel or area within the town that is actively used
for farming, livestock raising, irrigation or other agricultural purposes,
regardless of zoning designation.
   AGRICULTURAL OPERATION. The active use of land for the growing of crops,
raising of livestock or related activities, including irrigation, equipment use
and soil or water management practices typical of farming or ranching.
   AGRICULTURAL PRESERVATION AREA. An area formally designated to be preserved
for agricultural purposes, either through zoning, easement, policy designation
or state-recognized preservation programs.
   BUFFER. A physical space, barrier or landscape feature intended to minimize
conflict between agricultural and non-agricultural uses by providing
separation, screening or transition between land uses.
   CONFLICT MITIGATION. A process or set of conditions imposed by the town to
reduce adverse impacts or potential land use conflicts between agricultural and
non-agricultural uses, including fencing, drainage controls and access
accommodations.
   EXTERIOR IRRIGATION ACCESS. The requirement that head gates, ditches and
other irrigation infrastructure remain accessible to irrigation companies or
water users from outside a newly developed area, to preserve operational
integrity without requiring access through private lots.
   FENCE GRADE MEASUREMENT. The method of measuring the height of a required
fence from the finished grade of the newly developed property, used when
properties have differing elevations.
   HEAD GATE. A mechanical or structural device used to regulate water flow
from an irrigation ditch into a distribution system or agricultural field.
   IRRIGATION MITIGATION DOCUMENTATION. Written confirmation provided by an
irrigation company or water authority verifying the status, location and
required protection or relocation of irrigation infrastructure during
development.
   LARGE ANIMAL RIGHTS. The legal permission for property owners to keep
animals such as horses, cows, sheep or similar livestock on their land, subject
to applicable zoning and fencing standards.
   RIGHT TO FARM ANALYSIS. An evaluation conducted during the development
review process to assess potential conflicts with nearby agricultural uses and
identify mitigation measures to preserve farming operations.
   TAIL WATER. Water that runs off the end of an irrigated field, which must be
contained or managed to prevent flooding or erosion on adjacent properties.
(Prior Code, § 9.7.10)
§ 150.22 RIGHT TO FARM ANALYSIS.
   The Planning Commission, with the recommendation of the Building Official,
may impose restrictions on any development in order to protect:
   (A)   An existing agricultural area or activity;
   (B)   An agricultural or irrigation right-of-way or easement;
   (C)   An agricultural open space or agricultural preservation area;
   (D)   A zone that permits agriculture or large animals such as sheep, horses
or cattle; or
   (E)   Any property located within the town boundaries.
(Prior Code, § 9.7.20)
§ 150.23 MINIMUM MITIGATION.
   For any new development that is not located in an agricultural use area, the
following will be required, at a minimum, to mitigate the effects of new
development on the existing or potential agricultural uses.
   (A)   For all sides of the development adjacent to the agricultural
property, there is a minimum fencing requirement of a six-foot high NON-CLIMB
AGRICULTURAL FENCE, defined as a closely woven, two-inch by four-inch vertical
mesh with square deal knot fastening. Fencing must include one and seven-
eighths inch Schedule 40 or equivalent posts with a one and five-sixteenths
inch Schedule 40 or equivalent top rail.
   (B)   In order to provide adequate buffering, the Planning Commission and
Town Council may, on a case-by-case basis, require an upgrade to the fencing
and/or appropriate landscaping when the development activities will directly
interfere with the operations of the agricultural use.
   (C)   Where there is a difference in the grade of the properties on either
side of the required fence, the height of the fence shall be measured from the
grade of the property upon which the new development is located.
   (D)   The fencing requirements of this subchapter may be modified if the
developer obtains a written statement from the adjacent property owner
indicating that he, she or they are willing to modify or waive the fencing
requirements, as well as approval from the Planning Commission following review
by the Reviewing Department.
   (E)   For any new development that allows large animal rights that is
located adjacent to a development or zone that does not allow large animal
rights, fencing will be the responsibility of each individual lot owner to
ensure that his or her animals are properly contained.
   (F)   For fencing provisions, see §
154.082 of this code.
   (G)   A note shall be placed on the final plat that states: “This area is
subject to the normal, everyday sounds, odors, sights, equipment, facilities,
pests and any other aspects associated with an agricultural lifestyle. Future
residents shall also recognize the risks inherent with livestock.”
   (H)   A written statement shall be provided from the appropriate agency
regarding any irrigation channels, ditches, head gates and piping or any other
mitigation required.
   (I)   Exterior access shall be provided for all irrigation head gates as
directed by the applicable irrigation company. This may require relocation.
   (J)   During construction, access to all irrigation ditches and the
integrity of timely deliverance of irrigation water through all ditches shall
be coordinated with the applicable irrigation company.
   (K)   Adequate berming to retain irrigation tail water shall be provided.
(Prior Code, § 9.7.30)
§ 150.24 CONFLICT MINIMIZATION.
   (A)   The Planning Commission and/or Town Council may consider other actions
and site planning options to minimize conflicts between the proposed new uses,
buildings and structures and the existing or potential agricultural operations.
The goal of the town is to minimize or eliminate, to the fullest extent
possible, all potential conflicts and to assure a continuation of a right to
farm for the existing agricultural use without undue burden on the proposed new
development.
   (B)   The following issues shall be used to identify potential
incompatibilities and actions to minimize conflicts:
      (1)   Protection of irrigation access and maintenance of ditches and
canals;
      (2)   Safety and protection of the public from ditches, canals, ponds and
drainage systems;
      (3)   Safety and protection of livestock and farm equipment movement
corridors;
      (4)   Existing and proposed fencing on all agricultural property which is
adjacent to the proposed development;
      (5)   Erosion and soil protection and conservation concerns;
      (6)   Drainage of any development, including subdivisions, will be
designed to minimize the discharge or impact on agricultural lands and soils,
weeds, pests and household pet controls in subdivision areas;
      (7)   Provisions, acknowledgments and understandings by new property
owners of farm work hours and that farm operations may contribute to
objectionable noises and odors;
      (8)   Screening provisions and landscaping to reduce noise, odors, pests
or visual impacts for adjoining uses; and
      (9)   Any other provisions the Planning Commission and/or Town Council
consider necessary to protect the right to farm for agricultural uses,
operations and areas.
(Prior Code, § 9.7.40)
