**** GENERAL PROVISIONS ****
§ 151.01 DEFINITIONS.
   For the purpose of this chapter, the following definitions shall apply
unless the context clearly indicates or requires a different meaning.
   ACCESSORY STRUCTURE. A subordinate structure located on the same lot as the
primary building, such as a detached garage, barn, shed or greenhouse.
   APPLICANT. The property owner or the owner’s authorized agent who submits an
application for a permit, certificate or approval under this chapter.
   APPROVED PLANS. Building or site plans reviewed and accepted by the Building
Department or Planning Commission for compliance with applicable codes and
ordinances.
   AUTOMATIC FIRE SPRINKLER SYSTEM. A fire suppression system designed to
automatically detect and extinguish fires in accordance with applicable
building and fire codes, including IRC and state-adopted standards.
   BUILDING DEPARTMENT. The town’s designated administrative department is
responsible for overseeing building permits, inspections and code compliance.
   BUILDING PERMIT. An official approval issued by the Building Department that
authorizes construction or modification activities regulated by the State
Construction Code or local ordinances.
   DEVELOPMENT. Any construction activity, grading or land improvement that may
require a permit, site plan approval or zoning compliance review.
   FINAL PLAT. The final, surveyed map of a subdivision or land division
approved by the town and recorded with the county, which may include required
notes or disclaimers.
   GRADE (PROPERTY GRADE). The elevation of the ground surface at a specified
location, used to measure building height or fence height in relation to
adjacent land.
   NON-CLIMB AGRICULTURAL FENCE. A six-foot high fence constructed of two inch
by four inch vertical mesh with square deal knot fastening, supported by a one
and one-quarter inch Schedule 40 or equivalent posts and a one and three-
quarter inch top rail, designed to prevent animals or people from easily
scaling it.
   OCCUPANCY PERMIT. A permit is issued after all inspections are complete,
authorizing the use and occupancy of a structure in accordance with the
approved plans and applicable codes.
   PERMIT FEE. A fee charged for the issuance, review or administration of a
permit, established by resolution of the Town Council or under applicable code
provisions.
   PLANNING COMMISSION. The body appointed by the Town Council is responsible
for reviewing development proposals, site plans and zoning matters under
Chapter 150 and other related codes.
   RIGHT-OF-WAY. A publicly or privately held area reserved for transportation
or utilities, which may include streets, sidewalks, utility lines or drainage
channels.
   SELF-CONTAINED UNIT. A dwelling unit or trailer designed to function
independently with its own water, waste disposal and utility connections.
   SITE PLAN. A detailed drawing submitted as part of a permit or development
application showing existing and proposed buildings, structures, access,
utilities and other improvements required for review.
   STOP WORK ORDER. A formal order issued by the Building Department requiring
the immediate cessation of construction or related activities due to violations
of applicable codes or lack of permits.
   TEMPORARY DWELLING. A non-permanent residential unit authorized by the town
for use during the construction of a permanent dwelling on the same lot,
subject to specific conditions and time limits.
   TEMPORARY USE PERMIT. A permit that authorizes the temporary use of land or
structures for purposes such as construction staging, offices or park host
trailers, subject to town approval and conditions.
   UTILITY EASEMENT. A legally designated area on private property reserved for
public or private utility infrastructure (e.g., water, sewer, electricity).
   ZONING COMPLIANCE CERTIFICATE. A certificate issued by the Building
Department confirming that a proposed construction or land use activity is
consistent with the town’s zoning regulations.
(Prior Code, Title 9)
§ 151.02 ADOPTION OF STATE CONSTRUCTION CODES.
   The town hereby adopts by reference the State Construction Codes as
currently written and as amended from time to time by the state, including, but
not limited to:
   (A)   The International Building Code (IBC);
   (B)   The International Residential Code (IRC);
   (C)   The International Plumbing Code (IPC);
   (D)   The International Mechanical Code (IMC);
   (E)   The National Electrical Code (NEC);
   (F)   The International Energy Conservation Code (IECC); and
   (G)   Any other construction codes included in the State Construction Code.
(Ord. 2025-04, passed 5-21-2025)
§ 151.03 ADOPTION OF INTERNATIONAL FIRE CODE.
   The town hereby adopts by reference the current version of the International
Fire Code (IFC), as amended and adopted by the state, including any local
amendments as required to align with county fire standards.
(Ord. 2025-04, passed 5-21-2025)
§ 151.04 DESIGNATION OF OFFICIALS.
   (A)   The town hereby designates Sunrise Engineering (or its designee) as
the Building Official for the town, authorized to administer, interpret and
enforce the adopted construction codes.
   (B)   The town will hire a Code Enforcement Officer for the town, authorized
to enforce property maintenance codes, land use ordinances, nuisance
regulations and other town ordinances as directed.
(Ord. 2025-04, passed 5-21-2025)
§ 151.05 LIABILITY INSURANCE.
   The town shall provide liability insurance coverage for its appointed
officials, acting within the course and scope of their duties as required by
law.
(Ord. 2025-04, passed 5-21-2025)
**** BUILDING PERMITS AND OTHER REGULATIONS ****
§ 151.20 PERMIT REQUIRED.
   (A)   Any owner or owner’s authorized agent who intends to construct,
enlarge, alter, repair, move, demolish or change the occupancy of a building or
structure; or to erect, install, enlarge, alter, repair, remove, convert or
replace any electrical, gas, mechanical or plumbing system the installation of
which is regulated by the Building Code; or to cause any such work to be
performed, shall first make application to the Building Department and obtain
the required permit.
   (B)   Permits shall not be required for work exempt from a permit as
outlined in the adopted codes. Work exempted from a permit does not deem to
grant authorization for work to be done in any manner in violation of the
Building Code.
(Prior Code, § 9.1.10) Penalty, see §
151.99
§ 151.21 APPLICATION FOR PERMIT.
   A building permit shall be secured from the Building Department through
submission of an application accompanied by all required documents and fees.
(Prior Code, § 9.1.20)
§ 151.22 SITE PLAN AND DOCUMENT REQUIREMENTS.
   Upload the stamped site plan and required documents in PDF format to the
town’s website.
   (A)   Site plan. The site plan must include the following:
      (1)   Dimensions and setbacks of proposed structure;
      (2)   Location of a propane tank (if applicable);
      (3)   Location of the septic system, including the tank and drain field;
      (4)   Location of power lines and meter;
      (5)   Location, in feet, of the nearest fire hydrant (if over 700 feet,
an estimate may be used);
      (6)   Location and distance, measured in feet, from the property line to
the nearest town water line. If the distance is more than 1,200 feet, an
estimate may be used. Contact the Water Department;
      (7)   Location of all wells, whether they are in use or not;
      (8)   An appropriate descriptive legend, including north arrow, scale and
legal description;
      (9)   Name and contact information of the architect or engineer
responsible for the preparation of the site plan;
      (10)   The existing (or proposed) zoning;
      (11)   Dimensions, setbacks and height of all existing structures located
on the property;
      (12)   Measured dimensions of all recorded lot lines;
      (13)   Location of all existing and proposed drives and parking areas,
including types of surfacing, parking layout and dimensions;
      (14)   Show existing and proposed access roads, drives, turnout
locations, parking road width, rights-of-way and dedications (see the road
ordinance);
      (15)   Show all existing easements, vacated easements and rights-of-way.
A ten-foot utility easement along all roads must be shown;
      (16)   Must meet all required minimum setbacks;
      (17)   Locations, sizes and types of existing trees over six inches in
diameter (before and after proposed development);
      (18)   All proposed fences, screens and freestanding architectural walls,
including typical cross-sections and the heights above ground;
      (19)   Stormwater engineering (upon request), including existing and
proposed grading of the site, the location of existing and proposed utilities,
stormwater calculations for a 100-year storm, the detention area on-site that
will detain the 100-year storm; and
      (20)   Any other information required by the Planning Commission,
Building Officials, Fire Department or Town Council.
   (B)   Documents required.
      (1)   Warranty deed of trust for property;
      (2)   Copy of the record of survey filed with the County Surveyor’s
office;
      (3)   Boundary line agreement, if applicable; and
      (4)   Any other documents required by the Planning Commission, Building
Heads, Fire Department or Town Council pertinent to the proposed development or
building.
(Prior Code, § 9.1.30) (Ord. 03142023-1, passed 3-14-2023)
§ 151.23 APPROVAL OF SITE PLAN PROCEDURE.
   (A)   The site plan approval process shall include the following:
      (1)   Submit application to the town (www.fairfieldtown-ut.gov);
      (2)   Upload site plan and other required documents (PDF only);
      (3)   The Building Department will check that all required plans and
documents have been submitted;
      (4)   The Planning Commission will require a recorded survey and
subdivision plat, if applicable;
      (5)   The Planning Commission will review the site plan at the next
regular meeting; and
      (6)   The Planning Commission shall review the site plan and building
elevations. The Planning Commission shall confirm compliance with architectural
design, zoning and any other standards for buildings and structures to assure
compliance with the general plan and with the town’s generally applicable
policies and regulations.
   (B)   Once the Planning Commission is satisfied that all requirements have
been met, it will approve the site plan. The applicant may then apply for a
building permit.
(Prior Code, § 9.1.40)
§ 151.24 SITE PLAN AND DOCUMENT REQUIREMENTS FOR ACCESSORY BUILDINGS AND
ACCESSORY STRUCTURES.
   Upload the site plan and required documents in PDF format to the town’s
website.
   (A)   Site plan. The site plan must include the following (as applicable):
      (1)   Dimensions and setbacks of proposed structure;
      (2)   Dimensions, setbacks and height of all existing structures located
on the property;
      (3)   Statement of proposed use of structure as per the currently adopted
International Building Code;
      (4)   Location of propane tank(s) (if applicable);
      (5)   Location of septic system, including tank and drain field;
      (6)   Location of existing utilities, pipelines and transmission lines,
proposed utility lines;
      (7)   Location of the nearest fire hydrant in feet;
      (8)   Location of the nearest town water line, in feet, to the property
line;
      (9)   Location of all wells, in use or not;
      (10)   The existing (or proposed) zoning;
      (11)   Dimensions, setbacks and height of all existing structures located
on property;
      (12)   Location of all existing and proposed drives and parking areas,
including types of surfacing, parking layout and dimensions;
      (13)   Show all road width, rights-of-way and dedications (see the road
ordinance); and
      (14)   Any other information required by the Planning Commission,
Building Officials, Fire Department or Town Council.
   (B)   Documents required.
      (1)   Arsenic report (if there is an excavated foundation); and
      (2)   Any other documents required by the Planning Commission, Building
Heads, Fire Department or Town Council pertinent to the proposed development or
building.
(Prior Code, § 9.1.35) (Ord. 03142023-1, passed 3-14-2023)
§ 151.25 APPROVAL OF BUILDING PERMIT PROCEDURE.
   (A)   Submit building permit application to the town (www.fairfieldtown-
ut.gov);
   (B)   The Building Department will check that all plans, deeds, dedications
and any other required documents needed have been submitted and approved and
that the Planning Commission has approved the site plan;
   (C)   Pay estimated building fees to the town;
   (D)   The Building Department will submit plans and documents to a
contracted engineer for plan review and inspections;
   (E)   Once plans have been approved, the town will evaluate if any other
building permit fees need to be paid at this time;
   (F)   The Building Department will issue a building permit along with name
and numbers for inspections;
   (G)   Once all inspections are completed by the contracted engineer, the
Building Department will do a final review and inspection;
   (H)   Once final review and inspection is completed and any remaining fees
are paid, then an occupancy permit will be issued;
   (I)   The Building Department may revoke at any time a permit which has been
issued for any building constructed or being constructed, or which would be or
result, if constructed, in a violation of the Building Code or any ordinance of
this municipality; and
   (J)   Documents required:
      (1)   Stamped digital building plans;
      (2)   Proof of town-acceptable culinary water transfer or well permit,
state-approved culinary water transfer and point of diversion change or well
permit acceptable to the town;
      (3)   Septic system plan approved and signed by the county;
      (4)   Signed approval from Cedar Valley Fire Department;
      (5)   Contractors’ hold harmless agreement;
      (6)   Arsenic report;
      (7)   Any other documents required by the Planning Commission, Building
Heads, Fire Department or Town Council pertinent to the proposed development or
building; and
      (8)   Site plan signed and approved by the Planning Department.
(Prior Code, § 9.1.50) (Ord. 03142023-1, passed 3-14-2023)
§ 151.26 TIME LIMITS FOR USE AND BUILDING PERMIT APPROVAL.
   (A)   All use approvals, and all building permit approvals, shall be valid
for a maximum period of 180 days from the date of approval.
   (B)   If work has not commenced or a use or building established within 180
days from date of approval, the approval, permit or license, as required and
approved, shall be void and a new application, approval, permit or license
shall be required.
(Prior Code, § 9.1.60)
§ 151.27 VARIATIONS OF BUILDING PLAN PROHIBITED WITHOUT APPROVAL.
   No material, plan modification or use variation from the approved plan shall
be allowed unless such variations shall first have been approved in writing by
the Building Department or designee.
(Prior Code, § 9.1.70) Penalty, see §
151.99
§ 151.28 TEMPORARY DWELLING AND STORAGE STRUCTURES.
   (A)   Temporary dwellings incident to the property. The Building Department
may approve the use of a temporary dwelling incidental to the construction of a
one-family dwelling for a maximum of one year while building a home to live in
on the same lot, provided:
      (1)   A bond in lawful money equal to the cost of removing the temporary
dwelling, but not less than $1,000, is first posted with the town to guarantee
the timely removal of the temporary dwelling;
      (2)   The owner(s) of the lot and temporary dwelling agree to remove said
temporary dwelling within the time of the bond to obtain a full refund of the
bond or otherwise to allow the town to enter and remove the temporary dwelling
using the bond to defray costs;
      (3)   The owner(s) have obtained a building permit for a permanent
residential building;
      (4)   The temporary dwelling shall remain on the lot not longer than the
current term of the building permit for the single-family dwelling, the
completion date of the conventional dwelling or 365 days, whichever is less.
Exception: the Planning Commission may grant one extension period of an
additional 365 days upon finding that the construction of the permanent
dwelling is being carried out diligently toward completion; and
      (5)   The temporary dwelling unit shall be self-contained and the owner
must obtain a temporary dwelling permit to ensure that the temporary dwelling
is in compliance with the County Health Department, Building Code and with the
town’s requirements.
   (B)   Temporary storage structures. Temporary buildings and yards for the
storage of construction materials and equipment in any zone may require a
temporary use permit by the Planning Commission for a temporary office and
buildings and/or yards for storing vehicles, materials and equipment incidental
to a construction project. The permit shall be valid for a period of not more
than one year; the permit may be renewable throughout the length of the
project. The buildings shall be removed and the yard restored to its original
state upon completion of the project and expiration of the permit.
   (C)   Public park host trailer. In any zone, the Planning Commission may
issue a temporary use permit for a host trailer, provided:
      (1)   The host trailer is located on the same parcel of land as a
publicly owned or town-approved park site;
      (2)   The host trailer is removed from the park site when the terms of
the temporary use permit have expired;
      (3)   A permit must be obtained during each calendar year by the public
agency of the park; and
      (4)   The host trailer shall be self-contained, or approvals for water
and sanitary sewer shall be obtained from the County Health Department.
(Prior Code, § 9.1.80)
§ 151.29 PERMIT FEES.
   (A)   A fee for each building permit, electrical permit, plumbing permit and
fire permit shall be paid to the Building Official or Town Recorder/Clerk in
such amount as shall be established from time to time by resolution duly
enacted by the Town Council.
   (B)   Until such a resolution is adopted as to building permit fees, the
building permit fees set forth in the Uniform Building Code shall remain
applicable. The administrative and enforcement provisions of the Uniform
Building Code relating to building permit fees shall be deemed to apply to the
electrical and plumbing permit fees unless otherwise provided by resolution of
the Town Council.
(Prior Code, § 9.1.90)
§ 151.30 ZONING COMPLIANCE CERTIFICATE.
   (A)   Application. A zoning compliance certificate shall be secured from the
Building Department through the submission of an application accompanied by all
required documents and fees.
   (B)   Site plan and document requirements.
      (1)   Upload the site plan and required documents in PDF format to the
town’s website.
      (2)   The site plan must include the following:
         (a)   Dimensions and setbacks of proposed structure;
         (b)   Location of propane tank (if applicable);
         (c)   Location of septic system, including tank and drain field (if
applicable);
         (d)   Location of power lines and meter (if applicable);
         (e)   Location of the nearest fire hydrant in feet (if applicable);
         (f)   The location and distance, measured in feet, from the property
line to the nearest town water line, (if applicable);
         (g)   The existing (or proposed) zoning;
         (h)   Any other information required by the Planning Commission,
Building Officials, Fire Department or Town Council;
         (i)   Arsenic report (if there is an excavated foundation);
         (j)   Signed and approved site plan by the Planning Department if
there will be a permanent foundation; and
         (k)   If an agricultural building, a signed affidavit stating that the
structure shall be used for agricultural purposes only.
(Prior Code, § 9.1.95) (Ord. 03142023-1, passed 3-14-2023)
§ 151.31 STOP WORK ORDER.
   (A)   The Building Department or designee shall have the power to order all
work stopped on construction, alteration or repairs of buildings in the
municipality when such work is being done in violation of any provisions of any
state-adopted construction codes, any ordinance relating thereto or in
violation of the subdivision or zoning ordinances.
   (B)   Work shall not be resumed after the issuance of such order except on
the written permission of the Inspector.
   (C)   If the stop work order is an oral one, it shall be followed by a
written order within one hour. Such a written stop work order may be served by
any peace officer or other authorized person.
(Prior Code, § 9.1.100)
§ 151.32 ENTRY POWERS.
   The Building Department or designee shall have the power to enter into any
building or the premises where the work of altering, repairing or constructing
any building or structure is being performed for the purpose of making
inspections at any reasonable hour, pursuant to any of the provisions of this
code.
(Prior Code, § 9.1.110)
§ 151.33 CONSTRUCTION MITIGATION.
   The Building Department, or designee, has the power to assess sites where
construction has taken place or will take place and, at its discretion, to
require mitigation measures to ensure the safety of the public, property and
community.
(Prior Code, § 9.1.140)
§ 151.34 AUTOMATIC FIRE SPRINKLER SYSTEMS.
   The town hereby finds and determines that under certain conditions, an
automatic fire sprinkler system shall be installed in structures built in
accordance with the requirements of the International Residential Code, as
adopted in the State Construction Code, when any of the following divisions
apply:
   (A)   The structure is located in an urban wildland interface area, as
provided in the State Wildland Urban Interface Code, adopted as a construction
code under the State Construction Code; and does not meet the requirements
described in U.C.A. § 65A-8-203(3)(a) and State Administrative Code § R652-122-
200, minimum standards for wildland fire ordinance;
   (B)   The structure is in an area where a public water distribution system
with fire hydrants does not exist as required in State Administrative Code §
R309-550-5, water main design;
   (C)   The only fire apparatus access road has a grade greater than 10% for
more than 500 continual feet;
   (D)   The water supply to the structure does not provide at least 500
gallons fire flow per minute for a minimum of 30 minutes, if the total square
foot living space of the structure is equal to or less than 5,000 square feet;
   (E)   The water supply to the structure does not provide at least 750
gallons per minute fire flow for a minimum of 30 minutes, if the total square
foot living space exceeds 5,000 square feet but is equal to or less than 10,000
square feet; and
   (F)   The water supply to the structure does not provide at least 1,000
gallons per minute fire flow for a minimum of 30 minutes, if the total square
foot living space exceeds 10,000 square feet.
(Prior Code, § 9.1.150)
§ 151.35 VIOLATIONS.
   No person, whether as owner, lessee, sublessee or occupant, shall erect,
construct, enlarge, alter, repair, move, improve, remove, demolish, equip,
occupy or maintain any building or premises, or cause or permit the same to be
done, contrary to or in violation of any of the provisions of the applicable
sections of the codes adopted pursuant to this chapter or of any order issued
by the Building Official thereunder.
(Prior Code, § 9.1.160) Penalty, see §
151.99
§ 151.99 PENALTY.
   (A)   Any person failing to comply with the provisions of this chapter shall
be guilty of a Class B misdemeanor, and upon conviction therefor, shall be
subject to penalty. In all instances where the violation of this chapter is a
continuing violation, a separate offense shall be deemed committed on each day
during or on which the violation occurs or continues.
(Prior Code, § 9.1.160)
   (B)   A homeowner may be subject to a Class B misdemeanor if work requiring
a permit as set out in §
151.01 of this chapter is performed without first securing the permit(s)
required. Anyone who received payment or equivalent value to perform work
requiring a permit may be subject to a Class C misdemeanor if the work is
performed without first securing the permit(s) required.
(Prior Code, § 9.1.10)
