extent consistent with the Fire Code, the Knox key lock boxes and keys shall be
provided at locked entrances in order to allow emergency personnel access.
      (4)   Fencing. Tier 2 battery energy storage systems, including all
mechanical equipment, shall be enclosed by a seven-foot-high fence with a self-
locking gate to prevent unauthorized access unless housed in a dedicated use
building and not interfering with ventilation or exhaust ports.
      (5)   Signage. Signage on Tier 2 battery energy storage systems shall be
required as follows:
         (a)   The signage shall be in compliance with ANSI Z535 and shall
include the type of technology associated with the battery energy storage
system, any special hazards associated, the type of suppression system
installed in the area of the battery energy storage system and 24-hour
emergency contact information, including reach-back phone number;
         (b)   As required by the NEC, disconnect and other emergency shutoff
information shall be clearly displayed on a light-reflective surface. A clearly
visible warning sign concerning voltage shall be placed at the base of all pad-
mounted transformers and substations; and
         (c)   Signage shall be in compliance with §§
154.240 to
154.247 of this chapter.
      (6)   Noise requirements. Tier 2 battery energy storage systems shall
comply with all applicable town noise ordinances or codes.
      (7)   Buildings and accessory structures. All buildings and accessory
structures incorporated into any Tier 2 battery energy storage system shall use
materials, colors and textures that are of natural earth tones that blend the
facility into the existing environment; white, gray, silver and black are
acceptable colors for buildings and accessory structures as it pertains to this
section.
      (8)   Landscaping. Appropriate landscaping and/or screening materials
that are consistent with the fire safety compliance plans may be required to
help screen a Tier 2 battery energy storage system and buildings and accessory
structures from major roads and neighboring residences.
      (9)   Lighting. Lighting shall be limited to that minimally required for
safety and operational purposes and shall be reasonably shielded and downcast
from abutting properties. Cut-off lighting as required by the Town Lighting
Code may be required when determined necessary to mitigate visual impacts.
      (10)   Fire protection. Tier 2 battery energy storage systems shall have
a defensible space for fire protection with a fire protection plan, which will
be approved and signed off by the Fire Marshal.
      (11)   Local, state and federal permits.
         (a)   Tier 2 battery energy storage systems shall be required to
obtain all necessary permits from the State PSC, the State Department of
Environmental Quality (State DEQ), including the Division of Air Quality and
the Division of Water Quality, any applicable permits required by the town and
all applicable federal permits.
         (b)   A condition of approval of any conditional use permit for a Tier
2 battery energy storage system shall require the applicant to submit
reasonable documentation that the applicant has obtained all required permits
to construct the Tier 2 battery energy storage system from FERC, the State PSC
and the State DEQ prior to the issuance of a building permit. The town may
withhold approval of a building permit for a Tier 2 battery energy storage
system if such condition is not satisfied at the time the applicant applies for
such building permit.
   (I)   Standards of approval for a conditional use permit.
      (1)   Mitigation.
         (a)   1.   A conditional use shall be approved if reasonable
conditions are proposed, or can be imposed, to mitigate the reasonably
anticipated detrimental effects of the proposed use in accordance with
applicable standards set forth in this subchapter and with all other applicable
portions of this chapter.
            2.   If the reasonably anticipated detrimental effects of a
proposed conditional use cannot be substantially mitigated by the proposal or
the imposition of reasonable conditions to achieve compliance with applicable
standards, the conditional use may be denied.
         (b)   For the purposes of this section, the applicable standards which
shall be applied in assessing any application submitted pursuant to this
section shall be:
            1.   Whether the proposed use meets the applicable requirements for
conditional use of a Tier 2 battery energy storage system in the proposed zone;
            2.   The use is compatible, or with conditions of approval can be
made compatible, with surrounding uses;
            3.   The use is consistent with all applicable adopted town
planning policies and master plans; and
            4.   The reasonably anticipated detrimental effects of the proposed
use can be mitigated by the imposition of reasonable conditions.
      (2)   Limitations on conditional use approval. Subject to an extension of
time granted by the Planning Commission, no conditional use permit approved
pursuant to this subchapter shall be valid for a period longer than three years
unless a building permit has been issued or complete building plans have been
submitted to the Town Building Department within that period and the permitted
project is thereafter diligently pursued to completion; or unless a certificate
of occupancy is issued and a use commenced within that period; or unless a
longer period of time is requested and granted by the Planning Commission. Any
request for a time extension shall be required not less than 30 days prior to
the expiration of the three-year time period.
   (J)   Safety.
      (1)   System certification. Battery energy storage systems and equipment
shall be listed by a nationally recognized testing laboratory to UL 9540
(Standard for Battery Energy Storage Systems and Equipment) or an approved
equivalent, with subcomponents meeting each of the following standards as
applicable:
         (a)   UL 1973 (Standard for Batteries for Use in Stationary, Vehicle
Auxiliary Power and Light Electric Rail Applications);
         (b)   UL 1642 (Standard for Lithium Batteries);
         (c)   UL 1741 or UL 62109 (Inverters and Power Converters);
         (d)   Certified under the applicable electrical, building and fire
prevention codes as required; and
         (e)   Alternatively, field evaluation by an approved testing
laboratory for compliance with UL 9540 (or an approved equivalent) and
applicable codes, regulations and safety standards may be used to meet system
certification requirements.
      (2)   Site access. Battery energy storage systems shall be maintained in
good working order and in accordance with industry standards. Site access shall
be maintained, including snow removal, at a level acceptable to the local Fire
Department and, if the Tier 2 battery energy storage system is located in an
ambulance district, the local ambulance corps.
      (3)   Clearance and exposure. Battery energy storage systems, components
and associated ancillary equipment shall have required working space
clearances, and electrical circuitry shall be within weatherproof enclosures
marked with the environmental rating suitable for the type of exposure in
compliance with NFPA 70.
   (K)   Approval authority. The Planning Commission is the approval authority.
   (L)   Enforcement. Any violation of this section regulating battery energy
storage systems shall be subject to the same enforcement requirements,
including the civil and criminal penalties, provided for in the town’s zoning
or land use regulations.
   (M)   Appeals. See §
154.048 of this chapter for appeals provisions.
   (N)   Application to successors and assigns. 
      (1)   The terms of any conditional use permit issued pursuant to this
subchapter shall run with the land and be binding on any successor or assignee
of an applicant, owner or operator and any party that purchases and/or operates
a battery energy storage system.
      (2)   Any successor to or assignee of the original permittee of a
conditional use permit for a battery energy storage system shall provide its
name and mailing address to the town within 30 days after completion of such
transfer and shall provide replacement decommissioning security to the town
consistent with the requirements set forth in division (G)(1)(c) above.
      (3)   Each successor or assignee of the original permittee shall be
deemed the permittee under the conditional use permit from and after the date
of such transfer and shall comply with the terms of the conditional use permit
for the battery energy storage system.
(Ord. 2024-01, passed 4-11-2024) Penalty, see §
154.999
**** LANDSCAPE REQUIREMENTS ****
§ 154.225 PURPOSE.
   (A)   The purpose of this subchapter is to provide standards and
requirements for the installation of landscaping and screening walls for all
new and expanded development within the town in order to promote the general
welfare of the community; to effectuate attractive and logical development; to
aid in the enhancement of property values; to create an attractive appearance
along town streets; to compliment the visual effect of buildings; to provide
appropriate buffers between incompatible land uses and protection from intense
activities; and to aid in conserving water by encouraging the use of varieties
of plants, trees and shrubs indigenous to arid regions which are characterized
by low water consumption.
   (B)   The standards and regulations of this subchapter shall be held to be
the minimum requirements necessary for the promotion of the foregoing
objectives of this subchapter.
(Prior Code, § 10.19.10)
§ 154.226 DEFINITIONS.
   For the purpose of this subchapter, the following definitions shall apply
unless the context clearly indicates or requires a different meaning.
   CALIPER. The diameter of a tree trunk measured at a height of six inches
above the ground for trees up to four inches in diameter, and at a height of 12
inches for trees larger than four inches in diameter.
   DECORATIVE ROCK. Naturally colored stone or gravel used for landscaping
purposes, with a minimum aggregate size of one inch. DECORATIVE ROCK shall not
include decomposed granite, construction debris or gravel used solely for
vehicular access or utility coverage.
   DRIP IRRIGATION. A high-efficiency irrigation system that delivers water
directly to the base of plants through emitters, tubes or hoses, reducing water
waste from evaporation or runoff.
   DROUGHT-TOLERANT PLANT. A plant species adapted to arid or semi-arid
climates that can thrive with minimal irrigation after establishment. Includes
many native plants and xeriscape species.
   EVERGREEN. A plant or tree that retains green leaves throughout the year and
does not go dormant or lose its foliage seasonally.
   HARDSCAPE. Non-living landscape elements such as paved surfaces, walkways,
patios, retaining walls, fences and decorative structures that are integrated
into the landscape design.
   LANDSCAPE ARCHITECT. A person licensed by the state to practice landscape
architecture, including the preparation of landscape plans, grading, irrigation
design and plant selection.
   LANDSCAPE PLAN. A detailed drawing or set of documents prepared by a
licensed landscape architect showing existing and proposed landscaping,
irrigation systems, grading contours, plant materials, hardscapes and site
features as required by this chapter.
   LANDSCAPING. The combination of plant materials, groundcover, mulch,
decorative rock, fencing, irrigation systems and site design features is
intended to improve the aesthetic and environmental quality of a site.
   LIVE VEGETATION. Any living plant material, including trees, shrubs,
groundcover, turf or perennial plantings, used as part of a landscape design.
Artificial turf or synthetic plants do not qualify as LIVE VEGETATION.
   MULCH. A material such as bark, wood chips, compost or rock placed on soil
surfaces to retain moisture, suppress weeds and enhance visual appearance.
   NATIVE PLANT. A plant species that is indigenous to the state or the
Intermountain West region and is well-adapted to local soil, climate and water
conditions.
   ORNAMENTAL TREE. A small tree, often with distinctive flowers, foliage, bark
or branching, used for decorative purposes in landscaping.
   PARK STRIP. The area between a street curb and sidewalk, often planted with
grass, trees or decorative materials, and typically located within the public
right-of-way.
   SCREENING. A visual barrier created through fencing, walls, landscaping,
berms or a combination thereof, used to block undesirable views, provide
privacy or reduce environmental impacts.
   TURF. A surface layer of soil thickly covered with a mat of grass and its
roots, whether natural or synthetic. For the purposes of this chapter, TURF
refers only to natural grass.
   WATER-WISE LANDSCAPING. Landscaping practices that reduce water consumption
through the use of drought-tolerant plants, efficient irrigation systems and
design techniques that minimize water loss and runoff.
   XERISCAPING. A water-conserving landscaping approach that uses drought-
tolerant plants, mulch and efficient irrigation to create attractive landscapes
suited to dry climates.
(Prior Code, § 10.19.900)
§ 154.227 LANDSCAPING PLAN.
   All applicants for commercial purposes are required to submit a landscaping
plan. Landscape plans should achieve the following purposes:
   (A)   Preserve and complement the desert character of the natural landscape,
mitigate building and parking lot impact, add aesthetic charm, interest and
character and conserve water;
   (B)   Provide visual interest and variety;
   (C)   Provide necessary screening elements;
   (D)   Add year-round site beautification;
   (E)   Blend with the natural landscape;
   (F)   Highlight building design features; and
   (G)   Conserve water.
(Prior Code, § 10.19.20)
§ 154.228 LANDSCAPE REQUIREMENTS, RESIDENTIAL.
   All yards visible to the public must have an area the same size as the
square footage of the home that is improved, groomed and maintained. Examples
of this include xeriscaping, driveways, sidewalks, vegetation and trees which
are strongly encouraged.
(Prior Code, § 10.19.30)
§ 154.229 LANDSCAPE REQUIREMENTS, NONRESIDENTIAL.
   (A)   Improvements required.
      (1)   Landscaping plan submission. All applicants for commercial uses are
required by this chapter to make landscaping improvements and shall submit a
landscaping plan prepared by a licensed landscape architect to meet the minimum
landscape requirements outlined in this chapter. The Building Department will
review the submitted landscaping plan for compliance with this chapter and
forward the plan to the Planning Commission and Town Council for review and
action concurrent with development applications which require landscaping plans
to be submitted.
      (2)   Landscaping plan contents. The landscaping plan shall include, at a
minimum, the following information:
         (a)   The location and dimensions of all existing and proposed
structures, property lines, easements, parking lots, power lines, rights-of-
way, ground signs, refuse areas and lighting;
         (b)   The plant names (both botanical and common name), location,
quantity and size of all existing and proposed plants. The proposed plan should
indicate the size of the plant material at the time of planting and at
maturation. All existing vegetation that is to be removed or remain on the site
should be clearly identified;
         (c)   Existing and proposed grading of the site indicating contours at
two-foot intervals for grades that are 5% or greater. For areas where grades
are less than 5%, contours may be shown at one-foot intervals;
         (d)   Irrigation system plan;
         (e)   Existing and proposed fences and identification of the fencing
materials; and
         (f)   A summary of the total percentage of landscaped areas, domestic
turf grasses, deciduous and evergreen species and xeriscaping.
   (B)   Completion of landscape improvements. All required landscaping
improvements shall be completed in accordance with the approved site plan,
landscaping planting plan and irrigation plan and occur prior to the issuance
of a certificate of occupancy for the associated structure/building. Exceptions
may be permitted and certificates of occupancy issued where weather conditions
prohibit the completion of approved and required landscaping improvements. In
such cases, an extension period of not longer than six months is permitted and
a bond for not less than 110% of the total estimated value of the landscaping
shall be held until the project is in full compliance with this subchapter and
any approved site or landscaping plans.
   (C)   Planting standards. The planting standards are the minimum size of
landscaping that the town will accept towards meeting the landscaping required
in this subchapter. All planting must conform with the town soil ordinance. The
Planning Commission and Town Council shall use the planting standards in
evaluation of any landscaping plan. The following are planting standards for
required landscaping that shall be followed for all new development.
      (1)   Trees. Deciduous trees shall, when planted, have a minimum trunk
size of one and one-half inches in caliper measured eight inches above the soil
line. Evergreen trees shall have a minimum size of six feet in height. The
applicant may elect to use either deciduous or evergreen trees to meet this
requirement.
      (2)   Ornamental trees. All ornamental trees shall have a minimum trunk
size, when planted, of one and one-half inches in caliper measured eight inches
above the soil line.
      (3)   Shrubs. All shrubs shall be a minimum of one-gallon containerized
stock, when planted, that will attain a height of at least two feet.
      (4)   Turf. No landscaping shall be composed of more than 30% turf.
      (5)   Drought-tolerant plants. A minimum of 50% of all tree and shrub
species shall be required to be drought-tolerant.
      (6)   Weed barrier. Planting beds are required to have a weed barrier
with mulched wood chips, rocks or other similar treatment.
      (7)   Parking areas. Parking areas for vehicles, trailers and all heavy
equipment shall be weed-free.
      (8)   Other areas. All areas in front of screening, along frontage and
public roads, shall be weed-free with an aggregate size of three-fourths-inch
gravel to the depth of three inches, or any like material, and must be laid on
a minimum of two inches of road base.
   (D)   Design applications. The Planning Commission and Town Council shall
use the following design applications in evaluation of any landscaping plan.
      (1)   Selection of plants. Plants shall be selected for texture, form,
color, pattern of growth and adaptability to local conditions. Native plants
shall be preferred.
      (2)   Water conservation. All planter beds shall be irrigated through the
use of drip lines instead of spray heads to minimize water loss through
evaporation.
      (3)   Berming. Landscaped berming is required as a headlight screen or
buffer surrounding parking areas between different land uses, particularly
between nonresidential and residential uses or single-family and multi-family
uses.
   (E)   Required landscaping.
      (1)   Parking lot size. An area equal to 15% of the total size of the
parking lot must be landscaped.
      (2)   Building footprint. A minimum of the equivalent of ten feet
surrounding the footprint of the building must be landscaped.
      (3)   Visible sides. Each side of a building visible to the public or
neighboring residential property shall be landscaped.
      (4)   Trees per parking spaces. One tree for every ten parking spaces.
      (5)   Trees per square feet. A minimum of one tree shall be placed for
every 1,000 square feet of required landscaped area.
      (6)   Stormwater retention. Stormwater retention areas shall be
landscaped.
   (F)   Waiver. The Council shall have the authority to waive these standards
as circumstances dictate.
   (G)   Water-wise landscaping standards. The following are the minimum
standards for water-wise landscaping for any park strip, median or landscaped
area located within a public right-of-way or a commercial or industrial
development.
      (1)   Live vegetation area. At least 20% of the required landscape area
shall be live vegetation.
      (2)   Live vegetation integration. Live vegetation shall be distributed
throughout the landscape area and shall not be segregated.
      (3)   Rock material. Decorative rock material shall be a minimum of one-
inch aggregate and shall be at least three inches deep and be placed completely
on top of a weed fabric barrier that allows the permeation of water. Rock
materials shall not exceed the height of the sidewalk/trail or the top back of
the curb when placed along a public right-of-way.
      (4)   Drip irrigation. All water-wise landscaped areas shall be improved
with a drip irrigation system if applicable.
      (5)   Liability. Any individual, corporation or other entity shall be
responsible for any damage caused by landscaping in public rights-of-way,
including rocks or other materials that migrate onto a sidewalk, trail, street,
storm drain or other public facility, regardless of how such migration occurs.
(Prior Code, § 10.19.40)
**** SIGNS ****
§ 154.240 PURPOSE.
   The purpose of this subchapter is to establish sign regulations that enhance
the rural character of the town, maintain aesthetic consistency, ensure public
safety and minimize visual clutter while allowing appropriate signage for
businesses and developments.
(Ord. 2025-03, passed 5-21-2025)
§ 154.241 APPLICABILITY.
   Monument signs and wall signs are prohibited in all zones except for the
Light Industrial West Zone, Light Industrial East Zone and the Commercial
Overlay Zone. All signs must comply with the regulations in this chapter.
(Ord. 2025-03, passed 5-21-2025)
§ 154.242 DEFINITIONS.
   For the purpose of this chapter, the following definitions shall apply
unless the context clearly indicates or requires a different meaning.
   BANNER. A temporary sign made of fabric, plastic or similar flexible
material, typically mounted between poles, on a building or above an entrance,
used to announce events, sales or grand openings.
   BILLBOARD. A large, off-site sign structure designed for long-distance
visibility, typically used for commercial advertising not related to the use or
activity on the property where it is located.
   DARK-SKY COMPLIANT FIXTURE. A lighting fixture that is fully shielded and
designed to minimize light pollution by directing light downward and reducing
glare, in compliance with dark-sky preservation practices.
   DIRECTIONAL SIGN. A small, on-site sign intended to direct vehicular or
pedestrian traffic, such as “Entrance,” “Exit” or “Parking,” and not intended
for advertising purposes.
   EVENT SIGN. A temporary sign used to promote a special event, seasonal
activity or community gathering, and which must be removed shortly after the
event has concluded.
   EXTERNALLY ILLUMINATED SIGN. A sign that is lit by a separate light source
directed at the face of the sign, typically using shielded fixtures to minimize
glare and light trespass.
   FLASHING SIGN. A sign that contains or uses lights, LEDs or other sources
that blink, flash, scroll, change color or alternate in appearance.
   GOOSENECK LIGHTING. A style of exterior lighting fixture with a curved arm
that directs light downward in a focused and controlled manner, commonly used
to illuminate signage while preserving dark-sky principles.
   MONUMENT SIGN. A freestanding sign mounted on a solid base and constructed
close to the ground, typically not exceeding a height of eight feet. MONUMENT
SIGNS are designed to match or complement adjacent architecture using high-
quality materials.
   NEON SIGN. A sign made with luminous gas-filled tubing, often brightly
colored or animated. NEON SIGNS are generally prohibited except for limited,
window-mounted “Open” signs.
   PORTABLE SIGN. Any sign not permanently affixed to a building, structure or
the ground, including trailer-mounted signs, sandwich boards or signs on
wheeled platforms.
   ROOF-MOUNTED SIGN. A sign mounted on or above the roofline of a building or
structure, extending above the highest point of the roof.
   SANDWICH BOARD SIGN. A temporary, portable A-frame sign typically used on
sidewalks to advertise special events, sales or business openings.
   SIGN. Any object, device, display, structure or part thereof intended to
convey information visually and designed to attract public attention, including
words, symbols, graphics or illumination.
   TEMPORARY SIGN. A sign intended for short-term use, including banners, event
signs and promotional signage, that is not permanently installed and must be
removed after a specified time period.
   WALL SIGN. A sign that is attached flat against or painted directly on the
exterior wall of a building, and which does not extend above the roofline or
project outward more than 12 inches.
(Prior Code, § 10.21.15)
§ 154.243 GENERAL SIGN REQUIREMENTS.
   (A)   Monument signs.
      (1)   Each development is permitted one monument base sign per 500 feet
of frontage, which must comply with the town’s aesthetic and design standards
in the general plan.
      (2)   The maximum height shall not exceed eight feet, and the maximum
width shall not exceed ten feet.
      (3)   Materials shall be natural or complementary to the surrounding
architecture, including stone, wood or metal accents.
      (4)   Monument signs shall be externally illuminated with downward-facing
lighting. Internally lit or backlit signs are prohibited.
      (5)   Placement must not obstruct visibility for traffic or pedestrians.
      (6)   No advertising signs of any kind shall be allowed in any
residential zone, except signs pertaining to the sale or lease of residential
property and except for name plates or signs indicating the existence of an
office, a professional person or a home occupation.
      (7)   Exception: temporary signs (not posted longer than 72 hours).
   (B)   Wall signs.
      (1)   All wall signs must be included in the master development plan and
reviewed as part of the site plan approval process.
      (2)   Signs shall be proportional to the building’s facade and may not
exceed 10% of the wall area on which they are placed.
      (3)   Lighting shall be non-intrusive, such as gooseneck or downward-
facing fixtures.
      (4)   Signs shall be made of high-quality, durable materials and must
maintain a consistent aesthetic with the development.
   (C)   Directional and informational signs.
      (1)   Small directional signs, such as parking and entrance signs, shall
be limited to four feet in height. Maximum of 16 square feet.
      (2)   Signs must be consistent in color, material and style with the
primary monument sign.
      (3)   Internal illumination is prohibited; externally lit fixtures must
be shielded to prevent light pollution.
(Ord. 2025-03, passed 5-21-2025)
§ 154.244 PROHIBITED SIGNS.
   The following sign types are prohibited within the town limits:
   (A)   Digital, LED or flashing signs, including scrolling or animated
messages;
   (B)   Billboards or off-site advertising signs not associated with the
property;
   (C)   Roof-mounted signs extending above the highest part of the building;
   (D)   Portable or mobile signs, including trailer-mounted advertising;
   (E)   Neon signs, except for small window-mounted “Open” signs under four
square feet; and
   (F)   Signs obstructing road visibility or creating safety hazards.
(Ord. 2025-03, passed 5-21-2025)
§ 154.245 TEMPORARY AND EVENT SIGNS.
   (A)   Community event signs (e.g., town fairs, seasonal markets) may be
allowed but must be removed within seven days after the event.
   (B)   Banners and sandwich boards are permitted only for special events or
grand openings and must be removed within 14 days.
   (C)   Temporary signs shall not exceed 32 square feet in size and must be
securely fastened to prevent wind damage.
(Ord. 2025-03, passed 5-21-2025)
§ 154.246 LIGHTING STANDARDS.
   (A)   All sign lighting must use warm, non-intrusive illumination that
aligns with the town’s rural character.
   (B)   No neon, backlit or excessively bright lighting is allowed.
   (C)   Dark-sky compliant fixtures are required to reduce light pollution.
(Ord. 2025-03, passed 5-21-2025)
§ 154.247 COMPLIANCE AND ENFORCEMENT.
   (A)   All new signs must be reviewed and approved as part of the site plan
or master development plan process.
   (B)   Nonconforming signs must be removed or brought into compliance within
30 days of notice.
   (C)   Violations of this subchapter may result in fines, penalties or
removal of the noncompliant sign at the owner’s expense.
(Ord. 2025-03, passed 5-21-2025) Penalty, see §
154.999
**** PARKING ****
§ 154.260 DEFINITIONS.
   For the purpose of this subchapter, the following definitions shall apply
unless the context clearly indicates or requires a different meaning.
   FLOOR AREA RATIO (FAR). The ratio of the total gross floor area of a
building to the size of the lot on which the building is located. This term may
be referenced elsewhere in this chapter to regulate intensity of development.
   GROSS FLOOR AREA (GFA). The total floor area within the exterior walls of
all buildings on a lot, excluding unenclosed porches, terraces, garages or
other areas not designed or intended for human occupancy. GROSS FLOOR AREA
includes all floors (basement, mezzanine and upper stories) and shall include
enclosed storage, service, mechanical and utility rooms.
   LOADING BERTH. A designated off-street space or bay on the same lot as the
principal building or use, intended for the temporary parking of delivery
trucks or freight vehicles while loading or unloading merchandise, materials or
passengers.
   MANEUVERING SPACE. The area of a parking or loading lot required to enable
vehicles to turn, back or drive forward into or out of parking or loading
spaces, without encroaching on a public right-of-way.
   OFF-STREET PARKING. Parking spaces provided outside of a public street
right-of-way, designed and designated for vehicle storage to serve a specific
use or site. This includes associated drive aisles, access ways and landscaped
buffer areas.
   PAVED SURFACE. A finished hard surface treatment including asphalt, concrete
or approved pervious paving materials, designed to accommodate vehicle loading,
parking and traffic and to control dust and erosion.
   SCREENING. A method of reducing the visual and/or noise impacts of a land
use or structure through the use of fences, walls, landscaping, berms or
similar materials or techniques.
   SHARED LOADING FACILITIES. A condition where multiple businesses or tenants
on the same site or within the same building utilize one or more loading berths
jointly, provided such arrangement meets the total number of required berths
and operational demands as approved by the Planning Commission.
   USE, PRINCIPAL (OR PRIMARY). The main or predominant use of a lot or
structure, as distinguished from a secondary or accessory use.
   ZONING ADMINISTRATOR. The person designated by the town to administer the
zoning and land use provisions of this code, or their authorized
representative.
(Prior Code, § 10.23.60)
§ 154.261 RESIDENTIAL PARKING REQUIREMENTS.
   (A)   Off-street parking requirements.
      (1)   The following minimum number of off-street parking spaces shall be
provided and maintained by ownership, easement and/or lease for and during the
life of the respective uses.
      (2)   Parking within the front yard of a single residence use shall be on
or contiguous to a legal driveway.
      (3)   Grade/slope for residential driveways shall not exceed 8%. Anything
higher shall require approval from the Town Engineer.
   (B)   Requirements by dwelling type.

(Prior Code, § 10.23.10)
§ 154.262 NONRESIDENTIAL PARKING REQUIREMENTS.
   (A)   Plan required. Applications for a building permit for new
construction, additions, alterations or changes in use shall include a site
plan at an appropriate scale that clearly shows proposed site improvements
relating to parking as required by this section. All plans shall show the
location, arrangement and dimensions of off-street parking area(s), parking
spaces, parking lanes, points of ingress and egress, aisles/driveways, walls,
landscaping and barriers. Sidewalks, pedestrian ways, bicycle facilities and
their access shall also be shown. The access or driveway locations, width and
spacing, as well as sight lines and distances, the arrangement of spaces, stall
dimensions, surfacing, striping and lighting shall be in compliance with
adopted town standards.
   (B)   Lots within 300 feet of roads. All parking lots located within 300
feet of an improved town road shall be hard-surfaced with asphalt or concrete.
The material shall be approved by an engineer licensed by the state and be
capable of handling the anticipated size and weight of vehicles, including
public safety vehicles.
   (C)   Lots more than 300 feet from roads. All parking lots located more than
300 feet from an improved town road must be improved to the same standards as
the rural road.
   (D)   Variances. The Town Council, with the recommendation of the Planning
Commission, may make variances to these standards based on the following
circumstances:
      (1)   Public safety;
      (2)   Traffic;
      (3)   Consistency of surrounding use; and
      (4)   Proposed use.
   (E)   Stormwater management. All stormwater must be maintained on-site.
Parking lots and drive approaches may be required to be bordered with a curb
and gutter.
   (F)   Backing avoided. Parking lots shall be designed to avoid backing onto
a public street.
   (G)   Access. Except for approved on-street parking, access to any parking
space within a parking area shall be from a drive aisle and not directly from a
public street.
   (H)   Lots with more than one aisle. Parking areas with more than one aisle
must be so arranged that a car need not enter the street to reach another aisle
within the same parking area.
   (I)   Signage. Depending on circumstances, directional signs may be required
to differentiate between entrance and exit access points to the street.
   (J)   Grouping of spaces. Parking lots shall be designed in groupings not
larger than 200 spaces. Larger lots shall be divided by buildings, plazas or
significant landscaped areas oriented for pedestrian use.
   (K)   Within structures. The off-street parking requirements may be
furnished by providing spaces designed within the principle building or a
parking structure. However, no building permit shall be used to convert said
parking structures into a dwelling unit, living area or other activity until
other adequate provisions are made to comply with the required off-street
parking provisions of this section.
   (L)   Circulation between bays.
      (1)   Parking areas shall be designed so that circulation between parking
bays occurs within the designated parking lot and does not depend upon a public
street or alley.
      (2)   Parking area designs which require backing into a public street are
prohibited except with one-, two- or three-family dwellings.
   (M)   Adjacent development. Parking lot design shall consider development on
adjacent sites. The town may require cross-access connections/easements to
improve traffic circulation and to enhance public safety.
   (N)   Striping. Except for one-, two- and three-family dwellings, all
parking stalls shall be marked with painted lines not less than four inches
wide.
   (O)   Lighting. Parking lots used during the hours of darkness shall be
illuminated. Any lighting used to illuminate an off-street parking area shall
be so arranged as to reflect the light down and/or away from adjoining
property, abutting residential uses and public rights-of-way, and shall be a
maximum of 25 feet in height above the surface of the parking lot for
nonresidential uses and 16 feet for residential uses, and shall meet all other
regulations of outdoor lightning for the town.
   (P)   Protruding vehicles. All on-site parking stalls shall be designed and
constructed so that parked vehicles shall not protrude over a property line.
(Prior Code, § 10.23.20)
§ 154.263 OFF-STREET PARKING REQUIREMENTS.
   (A)   Space standards. Off-street parking spaces shall be provided according
to the following provisions and standards.
      (1)   Floor area. The term FLOOR AREA, for the purpose of calculating the
number of required parking spaces, shall be the GROSS FLOOR AREA of the
structures plus defined exterior use areas except as may be provided or
modified herein.
      (2)   Change of use or occupancy of buildings. Off-street parking and
loading spaces as required herein shall be provided at the time of any new uses
of land or construction of a new building. Any change of use or occupancy of
any building or buildings, including additions thereto, requiring more parking
shall not be permitted until such additional parking spaces as required by this
section are provided.
      (3)   Accessibility.
         (a)   Accessible parking for nonresidential developments shall be
provided in conformance with the Americans with Disabilities Act (ADA), being
42 U.S.C. §§ 12101 et seq., the State Americans with Disabilities Act (State
ADA), being U.C.A. Title 57, Chapter 21, and the International Building Code
(IBC), as amended.
         (b)   Accessible parking for multiple-family residential developments
shall be provided in conformance with the Americans with Disabilities Act
(ADA), Federal Fair Housing Act (FFHA), being 42 U.S.C. §§ 3601 et seq., and
International Building Code (IBC), as amended.
      (4)   Parking stall dimensions. The following shall be the minimum
parking stall size.
 
Type     Width   Length
Parallel 9 feet  25 feet
Standard 10 feet 20 feet
 
   (B)   Parking aisle dimensions. The following shall be the minimum parking
aisle width.
 
Parking Angle One-Way Aisle Two-Way Aisle
30 degree     18 feet       20 feet
45 degree     18 feet       20 feet
60 degree     18 feet       22 feet
90 degree     24 feet       24 feet
 
   (C)   On-site parking.
      (1)   Requirements.
         (a)   All parking shall be provided on-site. No parking shall be
permitted within any required setback or landscaped area.
         (b)   Each facility shall provide one parking space for each on-site
employee, with an additional amount of parking for drivers and visitors as
approved by the Planning Commission and Town Council.
      (2)   Minimum spaces. The minimum parking spaces required shall be two
per 1,000 square feet of gross building floor area. The Planning Commission may
require more parking spaces depending on building use.

(Prior Code, § 10.23.30)
§ 154.264 OFF-STREET LOADING REQUIREMENTS.
   (A)   Unless otherwise specified in this chapter, loading spaces or berths
shall be at least 45 feet in length, and all loading berths shall be at least
12 feet in width and 14 feet in height, exclusive of aisle and maneuvering
space and required parking space.
   (B)   Loading berths of 30 feet by ten feet for office use, motels and
hotels, restaurants, daycare centers, long-term care facilities and other
similar facilities may be provided for all or part of the required loading
berths if approved through the site plan approval process.
   (C)   Such space may occupy all or any part of any required yard space,
except front and corner side yards, and shall not be located closer than 50
feet to any residential zoning unless screened by a masonry wall not less than
ten feet in height. Loading spaces located in side yards shall not be visible
from a public street.
   (D)   Sufficient room for turning and maneuvering vehicles shall be provided
on the site so that vehicles shall cross a property line only by driving
forward.
   (E)   Each loading berth shall be accessible from a street or alley, or from
an aisle or drive connecting with a street or alley, without traversing a
residential zone.
   (F)   The loading area, aisles and access drives shall be paved so as to
provide a durable dust-proof surface and shall be graded and drained so as to
dispose of surface water without damage to private or public properties,
streets or alleys.
   (G)   Bumper rails shall be provided at locations where needed for safety or
to protect property.
   (H)   If the loading area is illuminated, lighting shall be deflected down
and/or away from abutting residential sites so as not to cause any annoying
glare.
   (I)   No regular repair work or servicing of vehicles shall be conducted in
a loading area.
   (J)   Off-street loading facilities shall be located on the same site with
the use for which the berths are required.
   (K)   If more than one use is located on a site, the number of loading
berths provided shall be equal to the sum of the requirements prescribed in
this section for each use. If more than one use is located on a site and the
gross floor area of each use is less than the minimum for which loading berths
are required, but the aggregate gross floor area is greater than the minimum
for which loading berths are required, then off-street loading berths shall be
provided as if the aggregate gross floor area were used for the use requiring
the greatest number of loading berths.
   (L)   Off-street loading facilities for a single use shall not be considered
as providing required off-street facilities for any other use.
   (M)   At the time of initial occupancy, major alterations or enlargement of
a site, or of completion of construction of a structure or of a major
alteration or enlargement of a structure, there shall be provided off-street
loading berth requirements. The number of loading berths provided for a major
alteration or enlargement of a site or structure shall be in addition to the
number existing prior to the alteration or enlargement.
   (N)   Space allocated to any off-street loading berth shall not be used to
satisfy the space requirements for any off-street parking facility.
(Prior Code, § 10.23.40)
§ 154.265 NUMBER OF SPACES REQUIRED.
   Unless otherwise provided in this chapter, every office, hotel, restaurant,
department store, freight terminal or railroad yard, hospital, industrial
plant, manufacturing establishment, retail establishment, storage warehouse or
wholesale establishments, and all other structures devoted to similar
mercantile or industrial pursuits, which have an aggregate gross floor area of
5,000 square feet or more shall provide off-street truck loading or unloading
berths in accordance with the following table.

(Prior Code, § 10.23.50)
§ 154.999 PENALTY.
   (A)   Any person violating any provision of this chapter for which no
specific penalty is prescribed shall be subject to §
10.99.
   (B)   Whosoever shall violate any of the provisions of this chapter shall be
guilty of a Class B misdemeanor and, upon conviction of such violation, shall
be punishable by a fine of not more than $1,000 or by imprisonment for not more
than six months in the County Jail, or by both fine and imprisonment as allowed
under U.C.A. § 10-3-703.
(Prior Code, § 10.1.25)
   (C)   (1)   A criminal violation under §
154.085 shall be a Class C misdemeanor.
      (2)   A civil violation under §
154.085 shall amount to $100 each day a violation occurs, each being a new
violation.
   (D)   (1)   Criminal violation. Any person who violates, disobeys, omits,
neglects or refuses to comply with any provision of §
154.110, or who knowingly permits or assists another in doing so, shall be
deemed guilty of a Class C misdemeanor.
      (2)   Civil remedy. The municipality may pursue civil remedies, including
fines, injunctions, abatement or other equitable relief permitted under the
town’s administrative code. The town’s enforcement officer is authorized to
enforce §
154.110 by issuing notice of violation, stop work orders or other
administrative actions, including recommending permit revocation when
necessary.
(Prior Code, § 10.11.260)
   (E)   Any person or entity who violates any of the provisions of §
154.208 of this chapter or who fails to comply therewith, or who violates or
fails to comply with any order or directive made thereunder, shall, severally,
for each and every such violation and noncompliance respectively, be guilty of
a Class B misdemeanor, subject to penalty as provided in division (A) above.
Furthermore, the imposition of one penalty for any violation shall not excuse
the violation or permit it to continue. All such persons or entities shall be
required to correct or remedy such violations or defects within a reasonable
time and, when not otherwise specified, each ten days that prohibited
conditions are maintained shall constitute a separate offense.
(Prior Code, § 10.17.100)
   (C)   Any person or entity who violates any of the provisions of §
154.210 or who fails to comply therewith, or who violates or fails to comply
with any order or directive made thereunder, shall severally for each and every
such violation and noncompliance respectively, be guilty of a Class B
misdemeanor, subject to penalty as provided in division (B) above. Furthermore,
the imposition of one penalty for any violation shall not excuse the violation
or permit it to continue. All such persons or entities shall be required to
correct or remedy such violations or defects within a reasonable time and when
not otherwise specified, each ten days that prohibited conditions are
maintained shall constitute a separate offense.
(Ord. 2024-01, passed 4-11-2024; Ord. 2024-14, passed 12-18-2024; Ord. 2025-03,
passed 5-21-2025; Ord. 2026-01, passed 3-25-2026)
